##### 1. Manual-deal per-phase pickup designation (G17 / SC-3 / Bishop `pickup` signal)

###### 1.1 Authoritative frontier (frame-agnostic — this is the allowlist source of truth)
The next-pickup tiles are ALWAYS the **front `count` entries of `state.Wall`**: `state.Wall[0 .. count-1]`. `state.Wall[0]` is the dice-determined break tile (ApplyBreakPointToWall rotates it to index 0); the frontier advances by `count` after each pickup. **Designate by TILE ID**, not by slot: ship `pickup.targetTileIds = state.Wall[0..count-1]`. Hicks allowlists EXACTLY those tile handles; every other wall tile rejects pointer/drag. This is correct regardless of the §F1 geometry question because a tile's rendered slot is whatever the translator placed it at (self-consistent).

###### 1.2 Per-phase table (ceremony order; WallBackDrawn = 0 throughout)
One interaction takes the WHOLE batch — never require N clicks for an N-tile batch.

| Phase | Picker (`pickup.seatIndex`) | count | cumTaken at entry | Frontier tile | Batch tile ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BreakPointMarked | dealer | 4 | 0 | Wall[0] | Wall[0..3] |
| PickupRound1 | dealer+1, +2, +3 (one seat per take) | 4 | 4, 8, 12 | Wall[0] | Wall[0..3] |
| PickupRound2 | dealer, +1, +2, +3 | 4 | 16, 20, 24, 28 | Wall[0] | Wall[0..3] |
| PickupRound3 | dealer, +1, +2, +3 | 4 | 32, 36, 40, 44 | Wall[0] | Wall[0..3] |
| SingleTilePickup | dealer, +1, +2, +3 | 1 | 48, 49, 50, 51 | Wall[0] | Wall[0] |
| DealerExtra | dealer only | 1 | 52 | Wall[0] | Wall[0] |
| → AwaitingDiscard | dealer (active) | — | 53 | — (wall INERT) | none |

- BreakPointMarked IS the dealer's Round-1 batch (`ExpectedPickupCount`=4); it then advances to PickupRound1 with picker = dealer+1. Round 1 = dealer + (dealer+1,+2,+3) = 16 tiles.
- Totals: dealer 4+4+4+1+1 = **14**; each other 4+4+4+1 = **13**; wall **55**. Matches §2.5.
- **DealerExtra draws the next FRONT tile (Wall[0])** — NOT a back/dead-wall draw. It is the dealer's first draw (§2.5). There is no dead wall (§2.6).
- Order is dealer → **counter-clockwise** (dealer+1 mod 4). DealService.dealOrder and AdvancePickupCursor agree.

###### 1.3 Physical (seat,col,layer) frontier + draw direction — ⚠ BLOCKED on F1
The physical slot of frontier tile `state.Wall[k]` = `WallOrdinalToSlot(breakOrdinal + cumTaken + k)` where
`breakOrdinal = WallDealerOriginOrdinal(dealer) + BreakPoint.TileIndex`, `WallOrdinalToSlot(ord) = (seat, col = local/2, layer = local%2)` seat-major over capacities [28,28,26,26].
**Draw direction:** increasing render-ordinal from the break, wrapping mod 108 = CCW from the break (seat-major dealer→dealer+1→…, col ascending, layer 0 then layer 1 within a stack).
**AMBIGUITY F1 (must resolve before SC-3 / any (seat,col,layer) allowlist):** BreakPointService computes `BreakPoint.TileIndex` in a **dealer-relative** wall-size frame `StacksPerWall=[14,13,14,13]` (dealer & opposite = 14 stacks), but `WallOrdinalToSlot`/`WallDealerOriginOrdinal` use a **seat-absolute** frame `[14,14,13,13]` (seats 0,1 = 14). These disagree for the break wall whenever the break wall ≠ the dealer's own wall, and for the dealer's own wall when dealer∈{2,3}. So `breakOrdinal` can mis-anchor the physical break vs the dice for many dealer×sum combinations (my live browser samples verified *contiguity* + one empty seat for dealer 0 only — NOT dice-anchor correctness). **Resolution (Bishop):** collapse to ONE canonical wall-size assignment (recommend adopting the seat-absolute [14,14,13,13] and refactoring BreakPointService to consume it, or vice-versa) so BreakPoint.TileIndex and WallOrdinalToSlot share a single frame; add a golden test asserting the emitted arc anchors on the true break for **every dealer × diceSum 2..12**. Until then, G17 keys on `targetTileIds` (§1.1) and is UNBLOCKED; SC-3 physical-endpoint realism is BLOCKED on F1.
**AMBIGUITY F2 (spec gap):** §2.4 says "count stacks" but never pins intra-stack draw order (top layer 1 vs bottom layer 0 first). Backend takes Wall[0],[1]… in list order; ordinal parity ⇒ layer. This oracle deliberately allowlists the whole target SET, so it is order-independent. If physical top-first realism is required for rendering, spec must pin it and the layer assignment verified.

---

##### 2. Per-seat entitlement model (SC-2 / G19 — Bishop opaque-handle projection)

**Reveal real tile identity to viewer seat V per location:**

| Tile location | Reveal real id to V? | Render |
|---|---|---|
| V's own concealed hand | **YES** | face-up |
| Another seat's concealed hand | **NO** | face-down opaque handle |
| Any discard (river), own or others' | **YES** (public) | face-up |
| Exposed meld — Chow / Pung / exposed Kong / added Kong (any seat) | **YES** (public) | face-up |
| Concealed Kong (暗杠) — V is the owner | **YES** | owner sees ids |
| Concealed Kong (暗杠) — V is NOT the owner | **NO** | face-down markers (§3.4.2) |
| Wall — any tile (incl. the manual-pickup target BEFORE it is taken) | **NO** | face-down opaque handle; id revealed to picker only AFTER the take moves it to hand |
| Hand-end / scoring reveal phase | reveal winner's hand + relevant per scoring | reveal |

**Current leak (must fix):** `ChangshaToAutotableTranslator.BuildThingEntry` emits every `things` entry **keyed by the real Changsha tile id 0..107 for all 108 tiles**, foreign hands and wall included — only `rotationIndex` differs (face-down). So the wire currently exposes every opponent's concealed hand and the full wall order; any client can read them. Bishop's projection must map **unentitled** tiles to per-viewer **opaque handles that carry no rank/suit identity** (the thing-index==tile-id 1:1 mapping is itself the leak vector), revealing real ids only for entitled tiles per the table. The manual-pickup **target** is an opaque interactive handle (`targetTileIds` may be per-viewer handles, not raw ids) — its identity is revealed to the picker only after the take.

---

##### 3. Discard-during-claim legality (FE-5 / G8) — CONFIRMED

**Confirmed CORRECT:** during an open claim window (phase `AwaitingClaim`), discard is blocked for everyone. `ChangshaGameStateMachine.Discard` opens with `RequirePhase(AwaitingDiscard)`, so any discard while `AwaitingClaim` throws (silently swallowed server-side today). While a Pung/Chow/Kong/Hu window is open the discarder has already discarded and the next seat has NOT drawn — no seat is in a discard turn until the window resolves (a claim is taken, or all pass and play advances). A seat holding a claim opportunity may ONLY claim or pass; it may not discard.
**UX contract (Hicks, FE-5):** surface the claim window (Pung/Chow/Kong/Hu/Pass + reason "resolve the claim first") instead of a silent discard no-op. Discard control enabled ⟺ `turn.awaitingDiscard && turn.activeSeat==mySeat` (phase AwaitingDiscard); claim controls enabled ⟺ an open window targets mySeat (phase AwaitingClaim); the two are mutually exclusive by phase. NOTE the still-open stale-claim bug: `EncodeClaimWindowClosed` is never called, so a resolved/passed window can leave claim controls live into the next discard turn — fix required so the exclusivity holds on the client.

---

##### 4. Lane deliverables
- **Bishop:** `pickup.targetTileIds[]` (+ optional `targetSlots[]`); call `EncodePickupCleared()` on ceremony exit and `EncodeClaimWindowClosed()` on window close (both currently comment-only); drop inbound `things` in ChangshaRuntime mode; opaque-handle projection per §2; resolve F1 (single wall-size frame + golden test all dealers×sums).
- **Hicks:** input allowlist = EXACTLY `pickup.targetTileIds` during the matching ceremony phase for my seat; all other wall tiles + auto mode + post-deal ⇒ inert (no hold/move/local-write/things-push); consume opaque handles; §3 discard/claim exclusivity + reason UX.
- **Hudson RED tests:** (a) auto arbitrary top-layer wall tile fully inert; (b) manual wrong-endpoint / wrong-phase inert; (c) manual right-endpoint (∈targetTileIds) → `pickup.take`, tile moves only via server response; (d) discard blocked during AwaitingClaim with surfaced reason; (e) pickup tombstone clears `isMyPickupTurn` post-deal; (f) entitlement: wire carries no real id for foreign hands / wall (opaque handles).

**Escalate to Vasquez before implementing past F1 or F2.**


### ═══ 2026-08-07 (continued 2) — BINDING G19/SC-2 opaque-handle CORRECTION (string handles, durable-identity reconnect-stable) + Vasquez R-1 §5 endorsement (merged 2026-08-07T08:1x; decisions in decisions.md §2026-08-07) ═══

### 2026-08-07T08-0x — BINDING correction: G19/SC-2 opaque-handle identity model (Ripley, integration coordinator)

**Supersedes** two conflicting statements: (a) my SC-2 "≥10^7 integer, per-(viewer,game) random permutation"; (b) Frost's G19 oracle "per-connection fresh". Coordinator binding resolves in favor of **durable player identity**.

###### Binding contract
- **Keyed by DURABLE viewer/player identity** (the reconnect-preserved `PlayerId` — the SAME durable identity BE-5 uses to reclaim a seat), **NOT per-connection**. **Stable across reconnect for the whole game lifetime** — the same player rejoining (new WS connection, same PlayerId) sees the SAME handles ⇒ render continuity. (This is why per-connection-fresh is wrong: it would rename every hidden tile on reconnect.)
- **Cross-viewer UNLINKABLE** — two players' handle spaces are uncorrelated; the same physical tile has a DIFFERENT handle per player.
- **Opaque STRING handles allowed/PREFERRED** (not large integers). Client distinguishes by TYPE/namespace: a string token ⇒ hidden ⇒ render a back, never infer typeIndex; a numeric `0..107` ⇒ real visible tile (own face-up hand / discards / exposed melds).
- **Server-SECRET keyed OR server-persisted mapping** — e.g. `handle = base64url(HMAC(serverSecret, gameId ‖ playerId ‖ realTileId))[:N]`, or a server-side persisted random bijection per (player,game). **MUST NOT be a client-known / brute-forceable derivation**: the tile universe is only 108, so any function the client can replicate (a plain hash of tileId, a fixed permutation, a monotone offset) is trivially invertible by enumerating 0..107. The server secret / persisted map is what defeats enumeration.

###### Enforcement (Bishop / Hicks / Hudson)
- **Bishop:** replace the ≥10^7-integer plan with **server-secret-keyed opaque STRING handles** keyed on durable `PlayerId`+`gameId`; reuse the BE-5 durable identity. Visibility-transition lifecycle unchanged (on take/discard/meld ⇒ tombstone the string handle + emit the real-tileId entry). Handles for the SAME tile must differ across players and be identical for one player across reconnect.
- **Hicks:** detect opaque by handle **type** (string), not a numeric threshold — `things` thing-index becomes `string|number`; render string-keyed things as face-down backs, never derive typeIndex from them; swap on the tombstone→real-id transition. (Numeric `0..107` ⇒ face `= key/4`.)
- **Hudson (P-1/P-4/P-5, raw-WS):** P-1 — hidden hand/wall keys are opaque strings, not real ids, AND not a brute-forceable transform of `0..107` (assert the same tile's handle DIFFERS for two players AND matches no trivial derivation); P-4 — reconnect with the SAME durable player identity ⇒ byte-identical handles (stable render); P-5 — two DIFFERENT players ⇒ uncorrelated handle spaces (no bijection recoverable).

Consistency note: SC-2 durable identity == BE-5 reconnect-seat identity == the reconnect-preserved PlayerId. One durable identity source across privacy + seat + reconnect. Relayed to bishop-1/hicks/hudson-1; acked to coordinator. No production edits by Ripley.

### G19 AMENDMENT (binding) — reconnect stability + string handles. Corrects "per-connection fresh" and SC-2's numeric key.

By: Frost (security/reviewer) · 2026-08-07 · **BLOCKING, pre-implementation.** TO: **Bishop, Hicks, Hudson, Ripley.** Amends the archived G19 oracle (decisions.md §2026-08-07T07-5x / decisions-archive.md) and refines coordinator **SC-2**. Reconciles a conflict Ripley flagged (P4/P5 same-viewer reconnect stability) AND corrects the handle key TYPE. READ-ONLY; no code.

##### Why this amendment
1. My original G19 said hidden handles are **"per-connection fresh (reconnect may re-mint)."** That CONFLICTS with Ripley's locked P4/P5 same-viewer reconnect stability. **Binding fix: handles are keyed on a DURABLE viewer identity and are STABLE across reconnect for the game lifetime.**
2. Coordinator **SC-2** currently specifies a **numeric** opaque key in a "reserved high space (≥10_000_000)". That does NOT meet the ≥64-bit requirement and a 108-value offset window is inference-fragile. **Binding fix: use a ≥64-bit opaque STRING handle** (numeric ≥2^53 loses IEEE-754 precision in JS).

##### Corrected handle contract (supersedes "per-connection fresh" and SC-2's numeric ≥10M)
- **Keying:** `handle = KeyedPRF(server_secret, durableViewerIdentity, gameId, physicalTileId)` — e.g. HMAC-SHA256(secret, identity‖gameId‖tileId) truncated, or a per-(identity, game) secret permutation encoded to text. `durableViewerIdentity` = seated `ChangshaSeatState.PlayerId` (survives reconnect) / a rejoining authenticated viewer id.
- **Type:** emit as a **STRING** (base64url/hex, ≥64-bit effective). The `things` collection key already accepts `string` (`Collection<string|number,V>`; relay uses string keys like `"current"`). **No numeric key ≥2^53** (JS precision loss ⇒ churn/collision). Reserved-namespace numeric offsets (SC-2 ≥10M) are REJECTED — insufficient width + inference-fragile.
- **Stability (P4/P5):** STABLE for the game lifetime for the same durable identity ⇒ reconnect re-derives the IDENTICAL handle→tile mapping (no churn, no reorder, own-hand actionability restored). `gameId` in the key ⇒ fresh per game (blocks cross-game deanonymization after a tile becomes public).
- **Unlinkability (P3):** keyed on identity (NOT connection) ⇒ different identities get independent, non-correlatable handles for the same hidden tile; same identity is intentionally stable. Position (slotName) correlation is public/allowed; identity correlation is impossible even for colluders.
- **Spectator caveat:** if an anonymous spectator's identity cannot be durably proven, a per-connection (unstable-on-reconnect) mapping is acceptable **for that spectator only** and MUST be documented in code + the PR. **Seated-player reconnect MUST be stable** — no exception.
- **Reconnect invariants:** a reconnect MUST NOT (a) reveal any newly-hidden→visible identity the identity wasn't entitled to, (b) reorder into a type-correlated mapping (stable re-derivation makes reorder impossible), or (c) break own-hand discard/pickup actionability.
- **Visibility transition:** on hidden→public/own, either (i) keep the handle and add the explicit identity field, or (ii) SC-2's tombstone-opaque + emit real-tileId entry — EITHER is acceptable **iff** the swap is atomic and the client bridges it for render continuity; visible tiles keying by real tileId 0-107 is fine (public/own identity is entitled).

##### Delta for each owner
- **Bishop:** switch SC-2's numeric ≥10M key to the ≥64-bit STRING, durable-identity+gameId-keyed handle above; persist the (identity,game)→permutation/secret for the game lifetime so reconnect re-derives identically; document any spectator fresh-mapping fallback. Keep entitled-only explicit identity + inbound handle-authority from the base oracle.
- **Hicks:** treat the `things` key as an OPAQUE STRING (no numeric ops, no `key/4`, no `key<108` arithmetic branch beyond "is this a real-tileId visible key vs opaque string"); render texture only from the explicit identity field; outbound actions send the string handle; bridge the visibility-transition swap for animation.
- **Ripley:** this satisfies your P4/P5 reconnect-stability lock (durable-identity keyed, game-lifetime stable) without weakening P3 unlinkability. Confirm the co-design LOCK (Bishop map ↔ Hicks resolve) adopts the STRING handle.
- **Hudson (add to the raw-WS oracle):**
  - **T6′ reconnect stability (seated):** seat S connect→capture own-hand identities + ALL opaque hidden handles; disconnect; reconnect SAME playerId+seat → assert the hidden-tile handles are BYTE-IDENTICAL to before (stable), own-hand identity/actionability restored, and NO newly-visible hidden tile.
  - **T6″ reconnect (anonymous spectator):** if no durable id, fresh mapping is allowed — assert it still leaks no identity (handles opaque, non-correlatable to the pre-disconnect set in a type-revealing way).
  - **T11 handle type:** every hidden key is a STRING, length/entropy ≥64-bit, and round-trips with no numeric coercion; assert no key is a JS number ≥2^53 and no key ∈ [0,107] for hidden tiles.
  - Keep T1–T10 from the base oracle (run against the LIVE backend).

##### Reviewer rejection thresholds (added; blocking G19)
- **R11 CRITICAL:** a SEATED player's reconnect churns/reorders hidden handles (breaks P4/P5) ⇒ REJECT. (Anonymous-spectator fresh mapping allowed only if documented.)
- **R12 CRITICAL:** numeric key ≥2^53 (precision loss) OR a reserved-offset numeric handle whose per-(viewer,game) permutation secrecy/entropy isn't proven ⇒ REJECT; require ≥64-bit STRING.
- **R13 HIGH:** reconnect re-mint produces a type-correlated mapping, or leaks a previously-hidden identity ⇒ REJECT.
- (R1–R10 from the base oracle stand.)

### DECISION (Vasquez) — R-1 §5 ENDORSEMENT of the SC-2 slot-key reconciliation (+ one binding caveat)

**By:** Vasquez (Rules oracle). **Date:** 2026-08-07T08:09. **Re:** Ripley D-2 (SC-2 privacy ⇄ R-1 pickup target). Feeds Bishop `pickup` signal, Hicks G17 allowlist, Hudson G4/G17.
**Status:** ENDORSED — consistent with the R-1 entitlement model. One BINDING implementation caveat below (non-obvious; must not be skipped).

##### Endorsement
Keying the client interaction match on `pickup.targetSlots[]` (the (seat,col,layer) batch) instead of `targetTileIds` is **correct and privacy-consistent**. A slot names a public POSITION, not a tile identity — everyone already sees the face-down wall geometry and the break location, so no SC-2/F-3 leak. `targetTileIds[]` stay per-viewer projected / reveal-only (never raw real ids to non-entitled viewers). Semantically identical to my R-1 §1.1 (set-membership over the designated front batch), re-keyed by slot. Reveal-on-take is per-viewer and matches R-1 §2: pre-take the target is opaque to all; on take the tile enters the picker's concealed hand → SC-2 tombstones the opaque wall handle + reveals the real id to the **picker only** (others still see a face-down hand tile).

##### BINDING CAVEAT (this is what makes slot-keying F1-robust — do NOT skip)
`targetSlots[]` MUST be captured in the **same translator wall-emission pass** that places the wall `things` — i.e., the slot strings emitted for `state.Wall[0..count-1]` in that exact loop — NOT recomputed from a second copy of the ordinal math. Because both the target and the rendered tile come from one projection, `hovered.slot ∈ targetSlots` is self-consistent **by construction**, so the allowlist is correct **regardless of F1**. F1 (dealer-relative [14,13,14,13] ↔ seat-absolute [14,14,13,13]) can shift the whole arc's anchor vs the dice — a VISUAL/SC-3 realism concern only — but the target's slot still equals where its own tile is drawn, so interaction never mis-targets. If `targetSlots` is instead derived independently, a divergence bug reintroduces the mismatch. **Forbidden: two code paths computing the target slot.**

##### Clarifications for the lanes
- **Server take is count-based/self-validating.** `pickup.take{seatIndex,count}` → `TakeTilesFromWall` consumes the front `count` of `state.Wall`; the client never selects *which* tiles. `targetTileIds` are NOT needed for server take correctness (authority = phase + seat + count); they exist only for the per-viewer post-take reveal/animation.
- **Batch = one action.** count=4 ⇒ 2 stacks = 4 slots (2 hoverable top layer-1, 2 occluded bottom layer-0). A press on any reachable top-layer target slot triggers the whole `count` take.
- **F1 golden test scope (Bishop):** assert the DICE-ANCHOR (break tile lands at the expected physical (seat,col,layer)) across ∀ dealer × diceSum 2..12 — that is SC-3 realism. Hudson G4's stack-level perimeter contiguity is necessary but weaker and will NOT catch anchor drift; keep both. Neither blocks G17, which is F1-robust via the co-derivation caveat.
- **Existing FE flag (from folded R-1):** `changsha-mode-policy.ts::changshaAllowsPointer` currently allows ANY wall tile during pickup — G17 closes it by restricting to `hovered.slot ∈ targetSlots` for the active pickup seat/phase only.

No production edits by Vasquez (rules oracle; read-only). Tombstones `EncodePickupCleared()`/`EncodeClaimWindowClosed()` confirmed present-but-uncalled → Bishop (D-3).

- Server (Bishop): `pickup.targetTileIds[]` for the PICKING viewer = the per-viewer opaque handles of `state.Wall[0..count-1]` (Wall[0] = dice break tile; advances by `count`). Per-viewer projected (non-picking viewers omitted/own-space).

Expressing the targets AS per-viewer handles satisfies BOTH — identity-based AND privacy-preserving. `targetSlots` is NOT the client match key (drop, or keep debug-only; unsound pre-F1). No real-id leak: handles carry no rank/suit; the picker learns which wall positions to click, faces revealed only on take (SC-2 tombstone→real-id).

- **G17 / FE-2 input allowlist: UNBLOCKED** — proceed now via handle matching; does NOT depend on F1.
- **SC-3 / G4 wall geometry-vs-dice realism: BLOCKED on F1** — Bishop must collapse to ONE wall-size frame ([14,13,14,13] dealer-relative in BreakPointService vs [14,14,13,13] seat-absolute in WallOrdinalToSlot; breakOrdinal mixes them ⇒ physical break mis-anchors vs the dice for many dealer×sum; contiguity verified for dealer 0 only, NOT dice-anchored) + golden test ALL dealers × sums 2..12. Lanes escalate to Vasquez before implementing past F1/F2.

own concealed hand; ALL discards (public); ALL exposed melds (chow/pung/exposed-kong/added-kong, public); concealed-kong to its OWNER only (others face-down); WALL = hidden to everyone incl. the manual pickup target pre-take (revealed to picker only after take); + scoring-reveal at hand-end. Everything else ⇒ per-viewer opaque handle carrying NO rank/suit. Leak vector confirmed: `BuildThingEntry` keys all 108 `things` by real tile id (only rotation differs) ⇒ wire exposes every foreign hand + full wall order.

### Frost review → Ripley: SC-4 manual-pickup schema must be G19-safe (targetHandles, not raw ids)

By: Frost (G19 security reviewer) · 2026-08-07 · **BLOCKING advisory on the FINAL SC-4 pickup schema.** TO: Ripley (schema owner), Bishop (server), Hicks (client). READ-ONLY; no code.

##### Current state (grounding)
- Server→client `PickupEntry` = `{ phase, seatIndex, count, dealMode, breakPoint{wallIndex,stackIndex,tileIndex}, wallIndex }` — POSITION/marker only, no identity. OK as far as it goes.
- Client→server take = `pickup.set('take', { seatIndex, count, wallTileIds })` where `wallTileIds` are **raw tile ids** the client PEEKS from its local wall (`emitTakePickup`→`peekNextWallTileIds`). **This raw-id path dies under G19** (wall tiles become opaque per-viewer handles; the client no longer knows raw ids) and is itself a G19 leak vector.

##### Advice (adopt in SC-4)
1. **Designation = explicit `targetHandles: string[]` — do NOT overload `targetTileIds`.**
   - Raw `targetTileIds` (0..107) would leak the identity of the upcoming wall tiles (`typeIndex = id/4`) to the picker AND any raw-WS reader → direct **P1** violation (reveals future wall order + tile faces).
   - `targetHandles` are the SAME per-(viewer,game) opaque STRING handles from the amended oracle that key the projected `things`, so they are **directly matchable** to what the client already renders (highlight/enable exactly those tiles) with ZERO identity. Per-viewer keying ⇒ two viewers get DIFFERENT targetHandles for the same physical target ⇒ no cross-viewer correlation (**P3**). Reconnect re-derives identical handles ⇒ designation still matches mid-pickup (**P4**).
2. **Slots/positions are DISPLAY-ONLY.** Keep `breakPoint`/`wallIndex`/slotName for the dealer marker/cursor (position is public), but the AUTHORITATIVE interaction + match key is `targetHandles`. Never resolve the pickup by slot alone (ambiguous/spoofable) and never let a slot/position field carry identity.
3. **Take (inbound) references `targetHandles`, server-resolved.** `pickup.take { seatIndex, handles: string[] }`. Server maps each handle→physical tile under THIS connection's namespace and REJECTS: handles outside the connection's namespace, handles ≠ the authoritative next-draw at the exposed end (wrong endpoint), wrong phase, wrong seat. Replaces the `wallTileIds` raw-id peek and closes the "any wall tile triggers pickup" input-boundary bug (G16/G17).

##### Reject thresholds (blocking; I will REJECT SC-4 / the impl diff on any of these)
- Any `targetTileIds` / raw id (0..107) in the designation OR the take ⇒ REJECT (P1).
- Same designation handle across two different viewers for the same physical target ⇒ REJECT (P3 cross-viewer correlation).
- Designation that permits interacting with a NON-designated wall tile / wrong endpoint (endpoint not server-enforced) ⇒ REJECT (input boundary).
- Any slot/position field carrying identity (typeIndex/tileId) ⇒ REJECT.
- A designation handle not matchable to a projected `things` entry the client holds ⇒ REJECT (unusable/desync).

Net: SC-4 = existing position/marker fields (display-only) **+ `targetHandles: string[]`** (authoritative, opaque, per-viewer, string per the G19 amendment); outbound take carries `handles`, not raw ids. Consistent with G19 P1–P5 + R1–R13. Frost holds the final diff review / RV-2 sign-off. No edits made.

### DECISION (Vasquez) — R-1 match-key reconciliation: handle-key CONFIRMED consistent; flag slot-key↔handle-key supersession

**By:** Vasquez (Rules oracle). **Date:** 2026-08-07T08:16. **Re:** Ripley refinement (pickup match key = per-viewer opaque handle of Wall[0..count-1]) vs the prior D-2 slot-key already in decisions.md §351. **Status:** handle-key ENDORSED for rules/entitlement; ONE consistency flag + one transferred caveat.

##### Confirmation (handle-key)
Binding the pickup match key to the **per-viewer OPAQUE HANDLE of `state.Wall[0..count-1]`** (`hovered.key ∈ pickup.targetTileIds(handles)`) is **consistent with the R-1 entitlement model AND with my F1-robustness requirement**:
- **Entitlement:** the handle carries no rank/suit — wall stays hidden to everyone pre-take; on take the tile enters the picker's concealed hand and the SC-2 visibility transition reveals the real id to the **picker only** (others still see a face-down hand tile). Matches R-1 §2 exactly.
- **F1-robust:** the handle is tile-IDENTITY-based (frame-agnostic), so it is the purest expression of R-1 §1.1 (`Wall[0..count-1]` frontier) — the interaction target never depends on (seat,col,layer), hence F1-independent. Correct that G17 proceeds without F1.
- **No leak from broadcasting:** the pickup entry targets only the picker's seat; non-picker viewers cannot match the picker's opaque handles against their own per-viewer wall handles, and the handles reveal nothing. Harmless.

decisions.md **§351 (Ripley D-2) currently records the SLOT-key** (`client interaction match key is targetSlots, NOT tileIds`). This refinement records the **HANDLE-key**. Both are rules-equivalent (set-membership over the same `Wall[0..count-1]` frontier; both preserve wall-opacity-until-take), but they are DIFFERENT implementations. **The lanes must implement exactly one**, or Bishop emits `targetSlots` while Hicks matches handles (or vice-versa) → silent no-match. `pickup.targetTileIds(handles)` MUST be the **exact same per-viewer handles used as the `things` keys** for `state.Wall[0..count-1]` in that viewer's projection — produced by ONE projection pass, not recomputed. ### Frost → Ripley: SC-4 count-based pickup (`targetSlots` len-1, no inbound trust) — **G19-SAFE (CONFIRMED)**

By: Frost (G19 security reviewer) · 2026-08-07 · Verdict: **CONFIRM G19-SAFE — no blocking objection.** Supersedes my earlier `targetHandles` advice FOR PICKUP (withdrawn — handles are unnecessary for pickup authority; Ripley is correct). TO: Ripley, Bishop, Hicks, Hudson. READ-ONLY; no code.

##### Why it's safe (grounded in current authority)
- `targetSlots` (length 1 = Wall[0] front) is a **public position** (`wall.*` slot name) — carries NO identity, NO handle, NO raw id. Position is inherently public/visible (the player sees the exposed end). ⇒ no P1 leak; no P3 cross-viewer identity correlation (both viewers share only the public front position, never a handle/id).
- Take is **count-based, server-authoritative**. `ChangshaGameStateMachine.TakeTilesFromWall` ALREADY enforces: `IsPickupPhase(phase)`, `PickupSeatIndex == seat`, `requestedCount == ExpectedPickupCount(phase)` (exact — a spoofed count throws), wall-underflow guard, then removes the FRONT `Wall[0..expected)` and appends to the seat's hand. The current WS handler derives `count` and IGNORES the `wallTileIds` VALUES (uses only the array length/count) → the client already cannot select a tile identity or an arbitrary count.
- ⇒ The client cannot choose tile identity, cannot draw out-of-order, cannot peek. Nothing inbound is trusted for SELECTION. This is STRICTLY SAFER than my `targetHandles` proposal (it removes the entire inbound handle-resolution surface). Handles are genuinely unnecessary for pickup — confirmed.

##### Binding conditions for the FINAL SC-4 (must hold; I'll REJECT the diff otherwise)
- **C1 — `targetSlots` is display-only public position.** Entries are pure `wall.*` slot-names with NO identity/typeIndex/id; used only to highlight the single UI trigger, matched to the client's projected (opaque) wall thing by POSITION. (WHICH physical slot is the true exposed end is the separate W-A/G4 wall-geometry gate — not a G19 concern.)
- **C2 — DROP raw `wallTileIds` from the outbound take.** The outbound `take` MUST carry only `count` (or nothing; server knows `ExpectedPickupCount`). Sending `wallTileIds` (today via `peekNextWallTileIds`) is a raw-id wire leak AND is impossible post-G19 (client no longer knows wall ids). Server keeps validating `count == ExpectedPickupCount`.
- **C3 — Client gates interaction to the single trigger only.** Pointer/drag enabled ONLY on the one `targetSlots` tile, ONLY in the correct pickup phase for the local seat; every other wall slot rejects with NO local mutation / NO optimistic move (wall-drag lockout, G16/G17). Taken tiles appear only via the authoritative `things` snapshot.
- **C4 — Server trusts NO inbound tile reference for selection.** Already true; keep it. If any `targetSlots`/id/handle field appears inbound, the server MUST NOT use it to select tiles (count + authoritative front only); reject wrong phase/seat/count as a silent no-op.

##### Scope note (this is a specialization, NOT a repeal of G19)
Inbound actions never need opaque handles: **pickup** = count/front (this design); **discard** = the owner's OWN entitled tile (own-hand real tileId, server-validated as in-hand + on-turn — no handle needed, no leak because opponents' tiles are opaque so a client can't even name them). ⇒ Opaque per-viewer handles are **OUTBOUND-projection-only**. The G19 requirement that hidden `things` (ALL wall tiles, foreign concealed hands, concealed kongs) be projected as opaque, per-viewer, non-inferable, reconnect-stable STRINGS (oracle P1–P5 + R1–R13, amended) STANDS UNCHANGED — that is the actual F-3 leak and is independent of the pickup take shape.

Verdict: **G19-SAFE, conditioned on C1–C4** (C2 is the only real change; the rest is already the authoritative behavior). Frost holds the final diff review + RV-2 sign-off. No edits made.

### SC-4 — FINAL IMMUTABLE Pickup Schema (Ripley, integration coordinator, 2026-08-07T08-2x)

**STATUS: IMMUTABLE. This is the single source of truth for the manual-pickup interaction.** It **supersedes and VOIDS** every prior pickup-key statement — decisions.md §351 "D-2 targetSlots", the handle-refinement, the "CANONICAL targetSlots" lock, and the "FINAL targetSlots" note. Where any earlier text disagrees, **SC-4 wins**. No further changes; lanes build against this.

##### Decision: match on OPAQUE PER-VIEWER HANDLES (not slots, not real ids)

###### Wire schema — `pickup` collection, singleton key `"current"`
```
PickupEntry {
  phase:      string            // ceremony phase (BreakPointMarked | PickupRound1..3 | SingleTilePickup | DealerExtra)
  seatIndex:  int               // whose pickup turn (0..3)
  count:      int               // batch size (4 for BreakPointMarked/Round1-3; 1 for SingleTile/DealerExtra)
  dealMode:   "auto" | "manual"
  targetHandles: string[]       // REQUIRED, THE MATCH KEY. The PICKING viewer's opaque per-viewer SC-2
                                //   handles for state.Wall[0..count-1], co-derived in the SAME per-viewer
                                //   projection pass that keys the wall `things`. Opaque strings; no rank/suit;
                                //   server-secret'd; durable-playerId-keyed (reconnect-stable).
  targetSlots?: string[]        // OPTIONAL, DISPLAY-ONLY (batch highlight/debug). NEVER the match key,
                                //   NOT authoritative (unsound pre-F1). Frontend MUST NOT gate on it.
}
```
- **No `targetTileIds`.** Real ids are NEVER sent in the pickup signal (that was the misnomer/leak risk). Post-take reveal happens through the `things` collection SC-2 transition (tombstone the opaque wall handle → emit the real-id concealed-hand entry to the picker only), not via pickup.
- **Clear/tombstone:** `EncodePickupCleared()` clears the `pickup` collection when the pickup phase ends (batch taken / phase transition). Wire it (exists at AutotableProtocol.cs:493, never called).

###### Client match (Hicks)
Wall thing is INTERACTIVE ⟺ `changsha ∧ dealMode==manual ∧ pickup.seatIndex==mySeat ∧ (in a ceremony pickup phase) ∧ hovered.thing.key ∈ pickup.targetHandles`. `hovered.thing.key` IS the SC-2 opaque handle string for that hidden wall tile — so the match is a direct string-set membership. One click emits the take for the whole batch; every other wall tile is non-interactive (no hover-select/hold/drag/sendUpdate/movement). Do NOT match on slots or ids.

###### Server take authority (Bishop)
Count-based / self-validating: `TakeTilesFromWall` consumes the authoritative front `count` of `state.Wall`. The server NEVER trusts a client-sent handle/id to decide what is taken — `targetHandles` is a client interaction gate + reveal/animation hint ONLY. A forged/misparsed handle cannot change what the server takes.

##### Requirement-by-requirement justification
1. **No raw real tile-id leak:** the pickup signal carries only opaque `targetHandles` (the SC-2 wall-thing keys already on the wire) + optional slot names. Zero real ids. ✓
2. **Frontend matches without physical-frame ambiguity (F1-survival):** handles are tile-IDENTITY based (a per-viewer projection of specific physical tiles); the match NEVER references `(seat,col,layer)`. F1 (wall-size frame / dice-anchor) only shifts the VISUAL arc placement (SC-3/G4) and **cannot** affect a handle-set match. Structurally F1-immune — no co-derivation *discipline* required for correctness (contrast slots, which are F1-safe only IF co-derived). ✓✓
3. **Same-viewer reconnect stable:** SC-2/G19 handles are keyed by durable playerId + gameId + server secret ⇒ identical wall handles and identical `targetHandles` after reconnect ⇒ stable match + render continuity. ✓
4. **Names/types unambiguous:** `targetHandles: string[]` (matches the SC-2 wall-thing key type = string). No `targetTileIds` misnomer. Bishop's wire field and Hicks's matcher reference the SAME named string[] ⇒ no silent no-match. ✓
5. **Server does not trust client identity:** count-based take (above); handles are gate+reveal only. ✓
6. **Pickup clear tombstone:** `EncodePickupCleared()` wired. ✓
7. **G19-survival:** `targetHandles` ARE the SC-2 opaque per-viewer handles — no new wire information, no rank/suit, server-secret'd (not brute-forceable over the 108-tile space), per-viewer (cross-viewer-unlinkable). Broadcasting the picker's handles is harmless (a non-picker cannot match them to its own handle space — Vasquez confirmed). ✓
8. **`targetSlots` disposition:** MAY remain as an OPTIONAL display-only field (batch highlight); it is NOT the match key and NOT authoritative. Preferred: omit it to remove all ambiguity; if kept, the frontend must ignore it for gating.

##### Reveal lifecycle (SC-2, unchanged)
Target wall tiles are opaque/face-down to EVERYONE pre-take (incl. the picker). On take, each tile enters the picker's concealed hand; SC-2 tombstones the opaque wall handle and reveals the real id to the PICKER ONLY (others see a face-down concealed-hand tile via their opaque projection). Scoring-reveal at hand-end.

##### F1/SC-3 note (unchanged, orthogonal)
SC-4 (interaction) is F1-independent and lands now. SC-3/G4 (wall VISUAL realism) remains blocked on Bishop's F1 fix (collapse to ONE wall-size frame [resolve dealer-relative [14,13,14,13] vs seat-absolute [14,14,13,13]] + backend DICE-ANCHOR golden ∀ dealer×sums 2..12; Hudson G4 world-coord contiguity is the weaker browser complement). Report F1 approach to Vasquez first.

##### Migration (small)
- Hicks: change `hovered.slot.name ∈ targetSlots` → `hovered.thing.key ∈ pickup.targetHandles`; drop the interim "any wall tile" fallback once `targetHandles` present; `changshaAllowsPointer(view, mySeat, pickupPhase, targetHandles)`.
- Bishop: emit `pickup.targetHandles` = the per-viewer handles assigned to `state.Wall[0..count-1]` IN the SC-2 projection pass (DRY — same handles as the wall `things` keys); remove any `targetTileIds`/real-id target; `targetSlots` optional display-only; wire `EncodePickupCleared`.

### SC-4 — FINAL, PARENT-LOCKED, IMMUTABLE: single-trigger-slot pickup

**STATUS: IMMUTABLE (parent directive). Broadcast once; no further changes.** SUPERSEDES and VOIDS every prior pickup statement: the `targetHandles` SC-4, all "batch-actionable / any-reachable-target-slot" language (mine + Vasquez's), `§351` D-2 `targetSlots(batch)`, the handle-correction, and the canonical-slots-lock. THIS is the sole authority.

##### Decision (parent, enforcing the user's original binding acceptance)
Manual pickup exposes **EXACTLY ONE interactable trigger tile** at the exposed wall end (`state.Wall[0]`). A single click on it triggers the **server-owned 4/1 batch**. The other 3 tiles of a 4-batch are NOT clickable. (User requirement: "only the exact server-designated next pickup tile at the exposed end of the smallest/current wall may be interacted with.")

##### Wire schema — `pickup` collection, singleton key `"current"`
```
PickupEntry {
  phase:        string           // BreakPointMarked | PickupRound1..3 | SingleTilePickup | DealerExtra
  seatIndex:    int              // 0..3 (active pickup seat)
  count:        int              // 4 (BreakPointMarked/PickupRound1-3) | 1 (SingleTile/DealerExtra)
  dealMode:     "auto" | "manual"
  targetSlots:  string[]         // EXACTLY ONE element = the trigger slot, co-derived for state.Wall[0]
                                 //   in the SAME translator wall-emission pass. The ONLY interactable tile.
  batchPreviewSlots?: string[]   // OPTIONAL, DISPLAY/ANIMATION-ONLY (the full 4/1 batch highlight).
                                 //   NEVER actionable; frontend MUST NOT gate interaction on it. Named
                                 //   differently on purpose so it can never be mistaken for the trigger.
}
```
- **NO `targetHandles`, NO `targetTileIds`** in the pickup signal. (SC-2 opaque handles still key hidden-tile RENDERING — orthogonal.)
- **Clear tombstone:** `EncodePickupCleared()` on pickup-phase end (exists AutotableProtocol.cs:493, never called — wire it).

##### Client (Hicks)
Wall tile INTERACTIVE ⟺ `changsha ∧ dealMode==manual ∧ pickup.seatIndex==mySeat ∧ (ceremony pickup phase) ∧ hovered.slotName === pickup.targetSlots[0]`. On click → send `pickup.take{ seatIndex, count }` — **NO tile id/handle/slot in the take** (zero client selection authority). ALL other wall tiles (incl. the other 3 in a 4-batch) are non-interactive: no hover-select/hold/drag/sendUpdate/movement.

##### Server (Bishop)
On `pickup.take`: validate `phase` + `seatIndex==active pickup seat` + `count==expected(phase)`; take `state.Wall[0..count-1]`. **IGNORE any client tile selection** (the take carries none). Emit `EncodePickupCleared()` after.

##### Why it survives F1
`targetSlots[0]` is co-derived for `state.Wall[0]` in the SAME wall-emission pass ⇒ it IS the slot the client renders `Wall[0]` into ⇒ `hovered.slotName === targetSlots[0]` is correct BY CONSTRUCTION, regardless of F1 (F1 only shifts the visual arc anchor = SC-3/G4). One trigger slot, one pass, no second ordinal-math.

##### Why it survives G19
The trigger slot is a **public POSITION** (wall geometry + break are already public) — no tile identity. The take carries NO id/handle/slot, so a malicious client **cannot** select a different tile; the server always takes the authoritative front `count`. No real ids on the pickup wire. Fully consistent with the BLOCKING G19 contract (SC-2 handles remain for rendering only).

##### Reconnect
`targetSlots[0]` is a fixed public slot name → stable across reconnect; no per-viewer projection needed for the pickup trigger.

##### Migration (small, from current diffs)
- **Bishop:** emit `pickup.targetSlots = [ Wall[0] slot ]` (single, co-derived) + `count`; optional `batchPreviewSlots` display-only; `pickup.take` validates phase/seat/count and takes `Wall[0..count-1]`, ignoring client selection; wire `EncodePickupCleared`.

Vasquez's corrected R-1 aligns with FINAL SC-4 (single exposed-end trigger; server takes Wall[0..count-1] atomically by count; Wall[1..count-1] NOT actionable). ###### Pin: `targetSlots[0]` = the reachable exposed tile at the draw frontier = the TOP-layer (layer 1) tile of the frontier stack
- **Why:** a wall stack is 2-high (`setup-slots.ts stack()` → layer 0 bottom + layer 1 top, with up/down links). `world.ts canSelect` blocks a tile whose `up` slot is occupied — so the bottom (layer 0) is NON-selectable while the top sits on it; and the raycast/hover hits the visually-top tile. - **Rule:** `targetSlots[0]` MUST be the slot of the **reachable, un-occluded tile at the current draw frontier** — the TOP-layer tile of the frontier stack while the stack is full (per canSelect, the tile whose `up`-link is empty). Slot form `wall.{frontierCol}.1@{seat}` (layer 1) for a full frontier stack.
- **F2 resolution (interaction):** whether the engine's flat `state.Wall[0]` maps to the top or bottom of the frontier stack is F2 (unspecified §2.4). The INTERACTION designation must resolve to the reachable TOP tile of that frontier stack regardless; the **take is unaffected** — server still takes `Wall[0..count-1]` atomically by `count` (batch semantics unchanged).

- `pickup.targetSlots`: string[] EXACTLY length 1 = the reachable TOP-layer frontier slot (co-derived in the wall-things pass). NOT the occluded bottom; NOT the batch; NOT `nextTileSlots`.

Vasquez's F1 hypothesis is CONFIRMED. The superseded `WallBreakOrdinal(wallIndex, stackIndex)` mixed
frames — render-absolute cumulative sizes `[28,28,26,26]` for the seat start + the engine's
dealer-relative `[14,13,14,13]` stack index — and drifted **exactly one stack (2 render ordinals)**
off the true break wherever the walls between the dealer and the break wall differ in size between
the two frames. Empirical sweep (old-anchor vs authoritative `WallDealerOriginOrdinal(dealer)+TileIndex`):

| dealer | dice sums that drift | note |
|--------|----------------------|------|
| 0 | 3 / 11 | your live browser sample only exercised dealer 0 |
| 1 | 3 / 11 | |
| **2** | **9 / 11** | worst seat — nearly always mis-anchored |
| 3 | 3 / 11 | |

Full 2d6 space: **56 / 144** (dealer × 36) combos drift, each by exactly 1 stack. Both the old and
new anchors are contiguous and land on the correct break SEAT — the defect is a 1-stack positional
error, so it looked "fine" under dealer-0-only inspection but is systematically wrong for dealer 2.

**Fix (already in #160, retained):** anchor the remaining-wall arc on the rules engine's authoritative
flat `BreakPoint.TileIndex` measured from the dealer's physical wall origin
(`WallDealerOriginOrdinal(dealer)`), so the mapping is faithful for every dealer with no frame mixing
and no dead clamp. **Golden test** (C-5/F1): `AutotableTranslatorTests`… actually

unchanged (no BreakPointService/DealService edits).

`BuildPickupEntry` now ships the designated batch instead of hard-coding `wallIndex=0` with no target:
```

```

  BreakPointMarked/Round1-3, 1 for SingleTilePickup/DealerExtra) — FRAME-AGNOSTIC tile ids.

### 2026-08-07T09-1x — F2 reachability SIGNED OFF (G17); adopt Vasquez's CLEAN fix (invert intra-stack layer mapping) — supersedes the "reachable-top-regardless" workaround

###### Sign-off
Vasquez SIGNED OFF F2 reachability for **G17 interaction** — my reachability lock resolves the dead-pickup blocker; G17 interaction is unblocked and stays GREEN regardless. Single-exposed-end semantic preserved.

###### The still-open artifact my workaround papered over (NON-BLOCKING for G17; REQUIRED for SC-3)
ROOT (Vasquez): `breakOrdinal` is ALWAYS even (dealerOrigin over caps [28,28,26,26] even; `BreakPoint.TileIndex = tilesBeforeWall + stackIndex*2` even) ⇒ `frontDrawn` parity == `cumTaken` parity, and `WallOrdinalToSlot layer = ord%2` ⇒ the engine consumes each stack **BOTTOM (layer 0) before TOP (layer 1)** — physically backwards.
- Batch-of-4 phases (cumTaken 0,4,8,… even, stack-aligned): take 2 whole stacks ⇒ grabbed top is among the 4 ⇒ no artifact.
- **Single-tile phases** (SingleTilePickup/DealerExtra; cumTaken 48,49,50,51,52): at EVEN cumTaken (48,50,52) `Wall[0]` is the OCCLUDED bottom while its top (`Wall[1]`) is still in the wall. A "trigger-at-reachable-top-regardless" patch grabs `Wall[1]` but `count=1` take removes `Wall[0]` (bottom) ⇒ **trigger ≠ take**, wall depletes bottom-out-from-under-top (orphaned/floating top). Invisible under opaque handles, but a real SC-3 realism defect.

###### Adopted CLEAN fix (supersedes the "regardless" workaround in ripley-sc4-f2-reachable-top-pin.md)
Invert the intra-stack layer mapping in `WallOrdinalToSlot` so the **LOWER flat index = layer 1 (top)**: even ord → layer 1, odd ord → layer 0. Then:
- `Wall[0]` is ALWAYS the reachable exposed tile (top while the stack is full; the exposed bottom once its top is drawn) ⇒ `targetSlots[0] = slot(Wall[0])` with NO "regardless" special-case.
- **trigger == take == Wall[0]** for ALL phases (single-tile included).
- Depletion is physically **top-first**; take stays count-based (`Wall[0..count-1]`).
§2.4 doesn't pin intra-stack order (F2) ⇒ TOP-FIRST is the rules-owned choice (Vasquez).

###### Gate assertions added (both gate Vasquez's SC-3 sign-off, alongside F1 dice-anchor)
- **G4 (Hudson):** TOP-BEFORE-BOTTOM depletion per stack — no orphaned/floating tile (the top leaves before the bottom). RED now (bottom-first) → GREEN after the inversion.
- **G17 (Hudson):** on a SINGLE-TILE pickup, the trigger tile == the tile that actually leaves the wall (trigger==take). RED now (even cumTaken mismatch) → GREEN after the inversion.
- G17 interaction (reachability) stays GREEN regardless.

#### SC-2 — G19 opaque per-viewer hidden keys — 📐 DESIGN v2 (binding clarification applied; coordinated pair)
Not landed yet: it breaks the bundle's `key//4` face derivation, so it lands with Hicks's client change.

**BINDING (Ripley override of 'per-connection fresh'):** handles are **per-viewer/player, stable across
reconnect for the same authenticated/rejoin identity during the game**, **unlinkable across different
viewers**, and the derivation MUST NOT be brute-forceable from client-known values (gameId + the viewer's
own playerId are CLIENT-KNOWN → a `Hash(gameId‖playerId)` permutation is invertible by that very viewer and
would leak the faces they aren't allowed to see). Use a **server-secret keyed mapping** or a **persisted
collision-safe map**. Prefer **opaque STRING** handles (no JS >2^53 precision loss).

Concrete backend contract I will implement on your go:
- **Handle type:** opaque **string** — `"h_" + base64url(HMAC_SHA256(serverSecret, gameId ‖ 0x1F ‖
  viewerIdentity ‖ 0x1F ‖ tileId)[:12 bytes])` (≈16 chars). REQUIRES `things` to accept string keys —
  **confirm with Hicks.** Numeric fallback if strings are impossible: map the same HMAC into a JS-safe
  `[10_000_000, 2^53)` window (still server-secret keyed) — strings preferred.
- **`serverSecret`:** a per-deployment secret **never sent to clients**, sourced/persisted like the JWT
  signing key (`Authentication:*`) so handles stay stable across a server restart too. NOT gameId/playerId.
  ⇒ a viewer cannot recompute the mapping ⇒ cannot invert `handle→tileId` ⇒ cannot deanonymize.
- **`viewerIdentity`:** the durable authenticated/rejoin player id (cookie `mahjong_pid` / auth subject),
  stable across reconnect — NOT the transient connection id.
- **Properties:** reconnect-stable (deterministic from the 4 stable inputs incl. the secret); unlinkable
  across viewers (independent HMAC per identity); collision-safe (96-bit output ⇒ negligible; I verify
  uniqueness within the viewer's ≤108 hidden set and re-derive with a counter on the astronomical collision);
  non-order-inferable (keyed on tileId, not wall position).
- **Equivalent alternative:** a **persisted** per-(game, viewerIdentity) random bijection → opaque tokens,
  generated once + stored (in-memory keyed store or a small table), looked up per snapshot. Same four
  properties; pick this if you want auditability over the stateless HMAC.
- **Hidden set (opaque handle, backs, NO face):** foreign concealed hands, ALL wall tiles, concealed kongs.
  **Visible set (real numeric `t` 0-107, face via `t//4`):** own face-up hand, discards, exposed melds.
- **`BuildThingEntry(V, t, S)`:** `key = VisibleTo(V,t,S) ? t : handle(serverSecret,G,V,t)`;
  `value = { slotName:S, rotationIndex:<faceUp|faceDown>, claimedBy, heldRotation, shiftSlotName }`
  (no `face`).
- **Hicks half:** treat a **string** `things` key (or `>=10_000_000` in the numeric fallback) as a hidden
  back (no `typeIndex`); derive face from `key//4` ONLY for numeric `key < 108`. Confirm key type + render
  rule and I land the backend + tests.
- **Lifecycle:** Changsha broadcasts are **full snapshots** (`full:true ⇒ map.clear()`), so hidden→visible
  is automatic (tile reappears under real `t`, stale handle dropped by the clear) — no explicit tombstone on
  that path; delta path emits `things[oldKey]=null` + `things[newKey]={…}`. A hidden tile keeps its handle as
  it moves slots (handle keyed on `t`, not slot).
- **RED tests I add (raw-WS, P-1..P-5):** hidden key ∉[0,107] & not `t//4`-derivable; visible resolvable;
  wall handles non-order-inferable; **reconnect-stable for same identity + unlinkable across viewers**;

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T09-40] hicks-fe6-g20-canvas-fill

### Hicks — FE-6/G20 canvas dead-space (letterbox) fix

**By:** Hicks (Frontend) · 2026-08-07T09:38 · Worktree `/tmp/mahjong-autotable-uat-frontend`. Self-contained canvas-sizing fix (separate from pickup/SC-2/geometry). tsc clean · 102 contract tests green · 0 new lint.

#### Root cause
`main-view.ts::updateViewport` sized the WebGL canvas to a FIXED `RATIO=1.5` (`renderWidth = height*RATIO` or `renderHeight = width/RATIO`), so the canvas was smaller than the viewport and the remainder was dead black — at 390×844 portrait the canvas was 390×260 (~584px black). The cameras were also pinned to `RATIO` (`PerspectiveCamera(30, RATIO,…)`, ortho frustum `w/(w/RATIO)`).

#### Fix (main-view.ts)
1. **`updateViewport`** now sizes the canvas to the FULL container (`renderWidth=width`, `renderHeight=height`, even-rounded) — canvas fills the viewport at any aspect, no letterbox/pillarbox bars. Then calls `updateCameraProjection`.
2. **NEW `updateCameraProjection(w,h)`** adapts the camera to the live aspect so a viewport-filling canvas isn't distorted:
   - Perspective ⇒ `camera.aspect = w/h; updateProjectionMatrix()`.
   - Orthographic ⇒ recompute the frustum to CONTAIN the reference table rect (aspect `RATIO`): container wider than table ⇒ fit height; narrower/taller (portrait) ⇒ fit width. Whole table stays visible (no clipping) with scene margin, never a black letterbox bar. Reduces to the original frustum at the reference aspect (landscape unchanged).
3. **`setupRendering`** re-applies `updateCameraProjection` after building a camera, so a perspective toggle keeps filling correctly.

#### Properties
- **Resize/orientation:** `updateViewport` runs every frame (`game.ts:150`) and re-fits on any live size change — portrait↔landscape handled.
- **Hit-testing preserved:** the camera projection now matches the canvas, so `MouseUi` raycasts stay accurate (affordances remain clickable) — also satisfies the earlier mobile hit-test ask.
- **Bonus:** also removes desktop-wide PILLARbox dead space (original clamped both axes to RATIO).
- Scene margin at extreme portrait is inherent framing (a ~square top-down table can't fill a tall viewport without clipping tiles) — distinct from the letterbox-bar seam, which is fixed. If a felt-colored margin is wanted vs the renderer's black clear, that's a scene-background/Ferro coordination follow-up, not the renderer seam.

#### Acceptance
Hudson's `red-responsive` (browser) asserts the canvas has no dead-space — my change makes the canvas element fill the viewport. No browser test added here (Hudson's lane; no overlap).

#### Files: `main-view.ts` (updateViewport fill + updateCameraProjection + setupRendering re-fit). No dist rebuild.

player identity:

- `playerId` = `AutotableConnection.PlayerId` — the SAME durable identity used for BE-5 seat reclaim and
  #153 reconnect (ONE identity source across privacy + seat + reconnect, as required).

  is brute-forceable — the secret is the whole point. Equivalent: server-persisted random bijection per

- Secret: defensive `ToArray()` copy + ≥32-byte enforcement (TESTED: short/empty rejected).

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T10-02] Frost-RV2-SC2-numeric-REJECTED-canonical-HMAC-string

### Frost RV-2 — SC-2 canonical decision: numeric-permutation REJECTED; HMAC string handles canonical. Integration review gated.

By: Frost (RV-2 / G19 sign-off) · 2026-08-07T09:51 · Per coordinator directive (numeric REJECTED). READ-ONLY.

#### State (verified across all 7 worktrees)
- Only ONE handle provider exists: bishop-2 `OpaqueTileHandleProvider.cs` (HMAC-SHA256 → base64url STRING), in `uat-backend-helpers`.
- EVERY `BuildThingEntry` still keys `things` by the raw `changshaTileId` (0-107) ⇒ **SC-2 is 0-HIT in every worktree** — no numeric OR string projection is wired yet. bishop-1's numeric-permutation scheme is not present/wired in any accessible worktree (uncommitted or in a lane I can't see).

#### Decision
- **Numeric-permutation SC-2 = REJECTED** (aligns with the coordinator + G19 amendment R12/P2). Rationale:
  1. **Precision/ambiguity:** a numeric handle either exceeds 2^53 (JS precision loss — forbidden) or lives in a small reserved window (e.g. 10M+) = low-entropy 108-value space; and a MIXED numeric keyspace (real id <108 vs handle ≥window) is discriminated by MAGNITUDE — fragile.
  2. **Statefulness:** a per-(viewer,game) permutation must be STORED for the game lifetime to be reconnect-stable; that mutable per-game state is error-prone. HMAC is STATELESS (deterministic from secret+viewer+game+tile) ⇒ reconnect-stable by construction.
  3. **Requirement:** the gate mandates a ≥64-bit NON-INFERABLE STRING. HMAC-SHA256 → 256-bit base64url string meets P2/P3/P4 cleanly; a numeric permutation does not.
- **Canonical = bishop-2 HMAC string `OpaqueTileHandleProvider`**, pending my **B1** fix (HKDF-derive the HMAC key from the supplied secret + DomainLabel; forbid raw-JWT reuse in the doc). See `Frost-RV2-review-OpaqueHandle-F2flip-HOLD.md`.

#### Canonical integration — I review ONLY AFTER both land
1. **Provider replacement:** remove any numeric scheme; wire the (B1-fixed) HMAC string provider into `BuildThingEntry` — HIDDEN tiles (ALL wall + foreign concealed hands + concealed-kong) → `DeriveHandle(durablePlayerId, gameId, tileId)` STRING key; VISIBLE (own hand + public discards/melds/claimed/revealed) → real numeric tileId + explicit face/identity. Reveal transition = tombstone opaque → emit real-id (atomic).
2. **Frontend mixed-key support (Hicks):** the `things` keyspace is now HETEROGENEOUS — numeric real-ids (0-107, visible) + opaque base64url STRINGS (hidden). Frontend MUST: treat the key as opaque (no `key/4`, no numeric/magnitude discrimination); render texture from the EXPLICIT identity field only (absent ⇒ render back); discriminate visible/hidden by the identity field's presence, not key type/magnitude; bridge the reveal tombstone→real-id for animation. Outbound: discard uses own real tileId (entitled); pickup is count-based ⇒ NO opaque handle sent outbound.

#### What I verify at the canonical review
- **Key source separation (B1):** dedicated OR HKDF-derived projection key; raw JWT/master key never the MAC key; secret ≥32B, defensively held, never logged.
- **Stability:** durable-PlayerId-keyed (reconnect re-derives IDENTICAL hidden handles), gameId-scoped (per-game fresh, no cross-game deanon); anonymous-spectator fallback documented.
- **Raw-WS P1–P5 (Hudson, live backend):** no hidden key ∈ [0,107] or numeric-derivable; cross-viewer **sharedBySlot** (same public slot, `key_A≠key_B`); public tiles share real id+face; own hand actionable (face present); reconnect (T6′) identical hidden handles for a seated player; alternate-field whitelist (face null, rotation fixed face-down, no new identity field, slot-canonical order). Thresholds R1–R13.

Until provider-replacement + frontend mixed-key both land, there is nothing canonical to sign — G19 stays 0-HIT/BLOCKING. Numeric scheme must be removed, not layered.

### Hicks — SC-2 frontend audit + adaptation (collection/key/types SAFE; render constraint reported)

**By:** Hicks (Frontend) · 2026-08-07T09:58 · Re: SC-2 integration active (hidden `things` keys → opaque HMAC strings). tsc clean · **109 contract tests green** · 0 new lint.

#### ✅ AUDIT — NO core collection library constraint (the wire/keys/types are SC-2-ready)
- `Collection<K extends string | number, V>` is generic over a `Map<K,V>` — string keys native. No `Number()`/`parseInt` on keys anywhere in `client.ts`.
- `base-client.ts` transports entries as a JSON **array-of-tuples** `[kind, key, value]` — JSON arrays **preserve element type**, so a numeric id stays a number and an HMAC handle stays a string across the wire (no object-key stringification). `dice`/`pickup` already ship `Collection<string|number>` in production, proving the path.
- `resolveTileFace`'s `⌊key/4⌋` is guarded behind `isOpaqueHandle(key)` (string early-return). `setup.ts i/4` is setup-time catalog indexing (not wire keys). `move-log Number(keyStr)` is the **claim** collection (seat), not `things`.

#### ✅ ADAPTED + TESTED (collection / key / types)
- `client.things: Collection<string | number, ThingInfo>`; all 4 `onThings`-family handlers string-safe (world partitions; move-log/replay/sfx filter to numeric; entries-loop guards `typeof==='number'`).
- **NEW pure `partitionThingEntries(entries)`** → `{real: [number,V][], hidden: [string,V][]}`, used by `world.onThings`. Keeps opaque handles OFF the numeric identity path (G19 invariant).
- `isOpaqueHandle` (type, not threshold) + `resolveTileFace` (string ⇒ face-down, never infer typeIndex; numeric ⇒ entitled `face`/`⌊key/4⌋`).
- **NEW contract tests:** mixed entitled + opaque snapshot partitions/resolves correctly; empty/all-one-type; **reconnect reconciliation** (a stable per-player handle re-partitions + re-resolves IDENTICALLY across a fresh full snapshot); reveal transition (opaque back BEFORE, entitled real-id face AFTER tombstone→real).

#### ⚠ RENDER-PIPELINE CONSTRAINT (needs a decision + co-sequencing)
The client pre-bakes **108 REAL Things** (ids 0..107, each a real `typeIndex`); the tile `InstancedMesh` is sized to the rendered set. An opaque handle has **no** pre-baked Thing, and a pre-baked `Thing[K]` **cannot** double as an anonymous back for a handle AND later render real id K (reveal-transition race/conflict). So hidden backs need render objects **not tied to a real id**:
- **(a) dedicated anonymous back-Thing pool** — reserved indices outside 0..107 + tile `InstancedMesh` capacity for the concurrent hidden set (~up to 95) + hide the non-visible pre-baked Things; or
- **(b) dynamic Thing creation** from the `things` stream (real key ⇒ face-up Thing, string key ⇒ anonymous back), dropping the static 108 pre-bake.

**Both need from Bishop:** the string-handle format, the **per-snapshot hidden set**, the **tombstone(handle)→real-id reveal event** shape, and slotName stability across the transition.

**CO-SEQUENCING RISK (flagging):** the moment Bishop emits string keys, hidden tiles (all wall + foreign hands) route to `onHiddenThings`, which — until the anonymous-back pipeline (a/b) lands — renders **no back mesh** (walls/foreign hands invisible). This must be landed together, or Bishop should gate string-key emission until the client back-render ships. Recommend **(a)** (smaller blast radius: additive pool, leaves the working numeric path intact) and a quick confirmation of the reveal-event shape so I can build + validate it against Bishop's wire.

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T10-21] Frost-RV2-SC2-WIRE-cert-emission-checklist

### Frost RV-2 — SC-2 WIRE cert (emission-level acceptance checklist for BuildThingEntry)

**Reviewer:** Frost (RV-2 — HANDLE/WIRE axis of the SC-2/G19 two-axis split).
**Interlock (locked with Vasquez):** Vasquez=SET (opaque-set ≡ §2-unentitled-set, two-sided ⊆/⊇ ∀ viewer×tile); Frost=WIRE (this doc); Edge(4 — no leak via alternate field/order) spans both; Hudson raw-WS P1–P5 = joint outcome proof.
**Status:** design-accepted, UNVERIFIED — `ChangshaToAutotableTranslator.BuildThingEntry` still emits `new CollectionEntry("things", changshaTileId, …)` (numeric key, SC-2 0-HIT). Cannot execute until canonical per-viewer projection lands.

#### Wire shape (grounded)
Entry = `CollectionEntry("things", KEY, ThingInfo)`.
`ThingInfo` = `{ slotName:string, rotationIndex:number, claimedBy:number|null, heldRotation:{x,y,z,w}, shiftSlotName:string|null, face?:number|null }`.
**The leak was the KEY** (= changshaTileId; frontend derives typeIndex = key/4), NOT `face`. The old `StripFace` (face→null) was cosmetic and insufficient.

#### The 7-item WIRE cert — for EVERY tile Vasquez marks opaque, the emitted entry must satisfy ALL:
1. **KEY = DeriveHandle(durablePlayerId(V), gameId, tileId)** — NOT changshaTileId. HMAC/HKDF, ≥256-bit, per-viewer-unlinkable, reconnect-stable, collision-free. [PRIMARY]
2. **face = null** (frontend `resolveTileFace` suppresses regardless; defense-in-depth).
3. **rotationIndex + heldRotation = canonical face-down**, NOT identity/type/draw-order derived (no orientation side-channel).
4. **slotName = canonical physical position only** (public geometry; SC-4 targetSlots[0] lives here — position public, identity hidden).
5. **claimedBy / shiftSlotName = null** for wall / foreign-concealed / 暗杠-to-non-owner (non-null only for genuinely public claim/shift state).
6. **ENTRY ORDER = slot-canonical**, never tileId/draw/deal/wall-order. (Frost's half of Edge(4): non-inferable keys still leak positionally if emitted in tileId/draw order.)
7. **Public/entitled tiles = numeric id + real face, IDENTICAL across viewers** (public tiles MUST correlate — correct, not a leak).

#### Precision A — reconnect-stability vs anonymity is NOT in tension (analyzed, sound)
A per-(V,tile) stable handle means at REVEAL time V retroactively learns H(V,T)=T and T's past trajectory. But at reveal T is ALREADY public and its past POSITIONS were always public (only identity is ever hidden). Retroactive de-anon exposes only already-public-at-reveal info ⇒ ZERO concealed leak. Stability is safe AND required (render/animation continuity across reconnect).

#### Precision B — reveal transition has TWO cases (2nd is bug-prone; joint SET+WIRE)
- **opaque→ENTITLED** (wall→V's own hand, or →discard/meld): tombstone(KEY→null) + emit fresh real-id entry. Clean.
- **opaque→opaque RELOCATION** (wall→FOREIGN concealed hand; 暗杠 formed, hidden to non-owner): tile MOVES but stays unentitled to V ⇒ MUST keep an opaque handle (same stable H(V,T), updated slotName), MUST NOT emit real-id. A projection that "reveals on draw" unconditionally LEAKS here. **Reveal ⇔ tile enters V's entitled set (Vasquez SET), never merely "a draw happened."**

#### Co-land / deferral
All 7 items are emitted by `BuildThingEntry`. Frontend security partition + face-rule are APPROVED + tested (45 contract tests) but `onHiddenThings` render is a documented stub. Whole SC-2 must co-land backend (projection) + frontend (render pipeline) before Hudson P1–P5 runs the joint proof.

#### Ping protocol
Frost pings Vasquez when (a) per-viewer things projection lands → SET cert + this 7-item WIRE cert both execute; (b) emission integrates → SC-3 production targetSlots/things golden (F1 44-table + F2 (a)+(b)).

#### Binding shape implemented
Full `things` snapshot = authoritative replacement, mixed keys: numeric = entitled real; string = opaque hidden handle (slot/rotation, NO identity). No per-tile tombstone — a reveal is "handle absent + numeric real present in the SAME full snapshot," reconciled atomically.

#### Pure core (tested) — `sc2-hidden-pool.ts` + `sc2-hidden-pool.contract.spec.ts` (6 tests)
- `reconcileHiddenBacks(hiddenEntries, prevHandles, full)` → `{place, release}` (stable reuse by handle; full-snapshot releases absent handles = the no-tombstone reveal).
- `reconcileRealVisibility(numericKeys, poolSize, full)` → `{show, hide}` (hide every pre-baked real absent from an authoritative snapshot).
- `physicalTileCount` invariant. Tests: **108 opaque wall**, **mixed own/foreign/public**, **handle→numeric reveal** (atomic), incremental-vs-full, **reconnect** (identical plan, no churn/leak), **no duplicate physical count** (shown reals + backs = 108 ∀ entitled∈{0,14,42,108}).

#### Render wiring — `thing.ts` / `world.ts` / (resize via `object-view.replaceThings`)
- **`Thing.hidden` + `hiddenHandle`** flags. `updateViewThings` and `canSelect` **skip hidden** Things → a non-entitled real never renders/raycasts (no leak); a free pool back is zero-cost.
- **Anonymous back pool:** 108 backs at reserved **contiguous indices 108–215** (sentinel typeIndex 0, one off-screen "hiddenpool@0" park slot, `hidden=true`). Added to `this.things` and `objectView.replaceThings` grows the tile InstancedMesh to **216** (108 real + 108 back). Idempotent; self-heals if a setup rebuild drops the pool.
- **`onThings(entries, full)`** now partitions and — only when SC-2 is active (a hidden handle present or backs assigned) — runs `reconcileHiddenBackPool` (place/reuse a back per handle at the server slot+rotation, face-down, no identity; release absent handles to the park slot) and `reconcileRealThingVisibility` (hide non-entitled reals, show entitled). `full` is delivered by the Collection. Reveal is one atomic snapshot: release the back + show the real → one frame, no duplicate/invisible.
- Backs are **raycastable via their slot** (placed, `hidden=false`) so the SC-4 manual pickup can target `targetSlots[0]`, but never discardable/flippable (wall group + the §D10 gate decide). Never face-inferred.

#### ⚠ Engine constraints found + handled (reporting)
1. **InstancedMesh instance index = `thing.index − startIndex`** ⇒ backs MUST be **contiguous** after the reals (108–215), not an arbitrary reserved base. Fixed (was 100000 → 108). Changsha = 108 tiles (ids 0–107); SC-2 is Changsha-only so no collision.
2. **Capacity derives from `this.things` via `replaceThings`** ⇒ I call it once when building the pool (→216); no static MAX to bump.
3. **`Thing` requires a non-null slot + `slot.thing` is single-occupant** ⇒ free backs park at a dedicated off-screen slot; a placed back vacates the (now-hidden) real from the target slot.
4. **`setup.replace` reassigns `this.things`** ⇒ `ensureHiddenBackPool` is idempotent + self-healing (re-adds + clears `handleToBack`).

#### NOT validated here (Hudson browser G17/G19): actual pixels (backs render face-down, uniform), real-pointer pickup on a placed back at `targetSlots[0]`, instanced capacity at 216 at runtime, and end-to-end against Bishop's real HMAC wire. Needs the running build + Bishop's emission (per-snapshot hidden set + full-replacement semantics).

`Privacy:HandleSecret` (dedicated master, base64) PREFERRED → else stable production JWT signing bytes used **only as HKDF IKM** inside the approved `OpaqueTileHandleProvider`, yielding a domain-separated projection key. **No raw HMAC.** Privacy mandatory/default-on for Changsha.

- **K-STABLE:** JWT signing bytes are production-stable (reused across restarts, else all JWTs invalidate) ⇒ handles are reconnect-stable across restarts — strictly better than the old per-process-random fallback. ✓

1. Provider = the ONE approved `OpaqueTileHandleProvider` (HKDF); ChangshaPrivacyProjector + OpaqueHandleService DELETED.
2. IKM resolution: dedicated `Privacy:HandleSecret` (≥32B) → else JWT bytes as IKM (NEVER raw MAC). In Production the JWT key is already fail-fast-required ⇒ fallback always present. In dev with neither: dev-only random (privacy still ON) or fail-fast — never raw ids.
4. Do NOT fall back to per-process random in Production (breaks stability) — JWT bytes are the production fallback.

Prefer the DEDICATED secret in production for blast-radius isolation (JWT-key-as-IKM couples a JWT-key compromise to handle derivation — though a JWT-key compromise is already total auth compromise, and HKDF prevents deriving the handle key from JWT signatures). ## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T10-58] hicks-sc2-key-format-confirmed

### Hicks → Ripley/Bishop — SC-2 key-format CONFIRMED (value-based discriminator landed)

**Re:** Ripley 10:44 — "HIDDEN `things` keys = `h_<22 base64url>`; VISIBLE tiles keep
numeric-string keys `"0".."107"`. Confirm your renderer branches on that."

**CONFIRMED — and I fixed a latent bug it exposed.** My original discriminator was
`typeof key === 'string'`, which would have wrongly treated a numeric-STRING visible
key `"0"` as an opaque back. That is now corrected to a **value-based** rule.

#### The discriminator (single source of truth: `changsha-mode-policy.ts::parseRealTileId`)

```
parseRealTileId(key):
  number  → key if Number.isInteger(key) && 0 <= key <= 107, else null
  string  → /^\d{1,3}$/ matched & parses to 0..107 → that number, else null
  → REAL tile  ⟺ parseRealTileId(key) !== null   (numeric OR numeric-string 0..107)
  → OPAQUE back ⟺ parseRealTileId(key) === null   (`h_…`, non-numeric, or out-of-range)
```

No `typeof` test. No numeric-threshold (≥10^7 / ≥2^53) assumption — those were older
superseded rules and are gone.

#### Where it is applied (all keyed on `parseRealTileId`)
- `isOpaqueHandle(key)` = `parseRealTileId(key) === null` — the back-vs-real gate.
- `resolveTileFace(key, face)` — opaque ⇒ `{faceDown:true, faceIndex:null}` (face NEVER
  derived from the key); entitled real ⇒ `face ?? Math.floor(realId/4)` where `realId` is
  the parsed number (works for `0` and `"0"` identically).
- `partitionThingEntries(entries)` — routes each entry to `real:[number,V]` (key
  **normalized to a number**, so world's numeric render/reconcile path is byte-identical
  whether the wire sends `0` or `"0"`) or `hidden:[string,V]` (`String(key)`).
- `move-log.ts` / `replay.ts` `onThings` — now filter+normalize via `parseRealTileId`
  instead of `typeof === 'number'`, so a numeric-string visible discard/meld is recorded
  (previously it would have been silently dropped) and no arithmetic is ever done on a
  handle.

#### Agreement with Bishop's projection
- VISIBLE: key int-parses to 0..107 ⇒ real tile, face = explicit `face` else `⌊id/4⌋`,
  fully actionable. Robust to key sent as number `0` **or** numeric-string `"0"`.
- HIDDEN: key `h_<base64url>` (or any non-0..107) ⇒ opaque back, render face-down,
  **never** infer typeIndex, raycastable for SC-4 manual target via `slotName` only.

#### Orthogonality preserved
SC-4 pickup interaction is unchanged and independent: still
`tileInDesignatedTrigger(hovered.slot.name, pickup.targetSlots)` (exact length-1,
fail-closed). Opaque handles are ONLY the hidden-tile RENDER/identity key — never the
pickup match key (per v4 FROZEN, `decisions.md:380`).

#### Validation
- tsc `--strict` clean.
- Browser-free contract suite: **132 passed** (was 129; +3 net new `parseRealTileId` /
  numeric-string cases in `changsha-mode-policy.contract.spec.ts`; SC-2 pool specs green).
- ESLint on changed files: `changsha-mode-policy.ts` 0 problems; `move-log.ts`/`replay.ts`
  carry only PRE-EXISTING eqeqeq/unused-import items outside my diff hunks — 0 new.

**Bishop:** you can emit either number or numeric-string for visible keys — my reader
handles both. Only requirement: hidden keys must be non-`0..107` (the `h_…` form is ideal).

**Still held for SC-2 final integration (unchanged):** Bishop HKDF projector + mixed
snapshots co-land, Hudson browser G17/G19, integrator dist rebuild. I am NOT rebuilding
dist or committing.

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T10-58] ralph-locked-privacy-config-3-deviations

##### 2026-08-07T10-40 (17:40Z): Ralph — locked privacy config vs current code: 3 deviations to fix (default-off, random secret, raw HMAC)

**Locked config:** privacy **default-on / MANDATORY for Changsha**; secret = **dedicated HandleSecret OR JWT bytes as HKDF IKM** (NOT raw HMAC); **no new required production secret**. Flag any default-off/disable or duplicate crypto.

**Current code (`AutotableWsEndpoint.cs:132-154`, `ChangshaPrivacyProjector.cs:53`) — 3 deviations:**

1. **🚩 DEFAULT-OFF** — `_opaqueHiddenHandles = runtimeOptions?.Value?.OpaqueHiddenHandles ?? **false**` (`:144`). Locked = **default-on/mandatory** for Changsha. A Changsha game currently emits NUMERIC keys (G19 leak) unless the flag is explicitly set. **Fix:** default-on (or force-on for Changsha, ignore the off path). **Flag any residual disable path.**

2. **🚩 WRONG SECRET FALLBACK** — `:147-153`: uses `HandleSecretBase64` if set, else falls back to **`RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32)` (per-process random)**. Problems: (a) NOT the locked **JWT-bytes-as-HKDF-IKM**; (b) a per-process random secret **breaks P-4 reconnect-stability** (handles change across process restart) **and multi-instance consistency** (each replica differs). The random fallback technically avoids a "new required secret," but the locked mechanism is **JWT signing-key bytes as HKDF IKM** — stable, already present in prod, no new secret. **Fix:** dedicated `Privacy:HandleSecret` if present, else **JWT bytes → HKDF IKM**; drop the random fallback.

3. **🚩 RAW HMAC (duplicate crypto)** — `ChangshaPrivacyProjector.cs:53` `HMACSHA256.HashData(_secret, …)` uses `_secret` directly as the HMAC key (no HKDF), and does NOT delegate to the HKDF helper. Locked = **not raw HMAC**; **delegate to `OpaqueTileHandleProvider` (HKDF-Expand/Extract)** which provides key separation. **Fix:** delete the projector's raw HMAC; delegate to the HKDF helper fed the IKM (dedicated-or-JWT).

**Net:** all three compose — `int-keysep` is satisfied ONLY when the projector delegates to the HKDF helper, fed a **dedicated-or-JWT-IKM** secret (not random, not raw HMAC), with privacy **default-on/mandatory**. No new required production secret (JWT IKM covers it).

**Tracking (g17_hold):** sc2-default-on(red, :144 default-false), sc2-secret-ikm(red, :153 random), sc2-projector-delegate(red, :53 raw HMAC), int-keysep(red, resolved-when-all-three-fixed). Monitor-only; no production edits by Ralph.

`Create(secret, gameId, viewerPlayerId)`:

- If the projector genuinely cannot be built, DROP hidden tiles or reject the connection — never fall back to real ids.
