using Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Auth;

namespace Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Autotable;

/// <summary>
/// K-STABLE seam — resolves the server-secret INPUT KEY MATERIAL for the mandatory Changsha
/// tile-handle privacy projection (SC-2 / G19). It selects a STABLE secret source so per-viewer
/// opaque handles survive process restarts, and it removes the former per-process random fallback
/// (which re-shuffled every viewer's wall/foreign handles on each restart).
///
/// <para>Precedence:
/// <list type="number">
///   <item><c>Privacy:HandleSecret</c> — a dedicated, base64, ≥32-byte secret (preferred: fully
///         decoupled from JWT key rotation).</item>
///   <item>Otherwise the STABLE configured JWT signing key bytes, used strictly as HKDF INPUT key
///         material — the projector HKDF-derives its own MAC key, so the raw signing key is never
///         used directly as a MAC key (key-level domain separation).</item>
///   <item>Otherwise (neither stable source): in Production THROW at boot (fail-fast — the random
///         fallback was removed); in non-Production defer to the existing auth-key convention (the
///         JWT provider's dev key) rather than minting a privacy-specific random.</item>
/// </list></para>
///
/// <para>Never used as the MAC key directly and never logged; the returned bytes are HKDF INPUT
/// only (see <see cref="OpaqueTileHandleProvider"/>).</para>
/// </summary>
internal static class ChangshaHandleSecretSource
{
    /// <summary>
    /// B-DEFAULT — decides whether the mandatory Changsha tile-handle privacy projection is active
    /// for this process. Privacy is DEFAULT-ON and Production forces it on regardless of
    /// <paramref name="configuredOpaqueHiddenHandles"/> (there is no shippable disable gate); the
    /// flag can only turn privacy off in NON-Production, as an in-process test seam.
    /// </summary>
    public static bool IsPrivacyOn(bool configuredOpaqueHiddenHandles, bool isProduction)
        => isProduction || configuredOpaqueHiddenHandles;

    /// <summary>Operator-actionable Production failure message (emitted verbatim; tests hard-assert it).</summary>
    public const string ProductionRequiresStableSecretMessage =
        "Changsha tile-handle privacy is mandatory but no STABLE server secret is configured in " +
        "Production. Set Privacy:HandleSecret=<base64, >=32 bytes> (preferred) OR a stable " +
        "Authentication__JwtSigningKeys__0=<base64 key> so opaque per-viewer handles survive " +
        "container restarts. The per-process random fallback was removed. See docs/jwt-rotation.md §7.";

    /// <summary>
    /// Resolves the HKDF input key material for the handle projection, or throws
    /// <see cref="InvalidOperationException"/> in Production when neither a dedicated
    /// <c>Privacy:HandleSecret</c> nor a stable configured JWT signing key exists.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="handleSecretBase64">Value of <c>Privacy:HandleSecret</c> (may be null/empty).</param>
    /// <param name="jwtSigningKeys">The process JWT signing key provider (its active HMAC key is the
    /// stable fallback source; its ephemeral-fallback flag distinguishes a configured key from the
    /// dev auto-mint).</param>
    /// <param name="isProduction"><see langword="true"/> under <c>ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production</c>.</param>
    public static byte[] ResolveIkm(string? handleSecretBase64, JwtSigningKeyProvider jwtSigningKeys, bool isProduction)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(jwtSigningKeys);

        // 1) Dedicated Privacy:HandleSecret — preferred when present and long enough.
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(handleSecretBase64))
        {
            byte[]? decoded = null;
            try { decoded = Convert.FromBase64String(handleSecretBase64.Trim()); }
            catch (FormatException) { decoded = null; }
            if (decoded is { Length: >= OpaqueTileHandleProvider.MinimumSecretLengthBytes })
            {
                return decoded;
            }
            // A present-but-unusable value (bad base64 / too short) is an operator error; fall
            // through to the JWT key so it degrades to the next stable source rather than crashing,
            // and Production still fails below if that source is also unstable.
        }

        // 2) STABLE configured JWT signing key bytes as HKDF IKM (never used directly as a MAC key).
        if (!jwtSigningKeys.UsingEphemeralFallbackKey)
        {
            var configured = jwtSigningKeys.ActiveKey.Material;
            if (configured.Length >= OpaqueTileHandleProvider.MinimumSecretLengthBytes)
            {
                return configured;
            }
            // A stable but too-short operator key cannot back a 256-bit handle space — treat as
            // "no usable stable source" and fall through to the environment branch.
        }

        // 3) No stable source. Production fails fast; non-Production follows the existing auth-key
        //    convention (the provider's dev key) instead of a privacy-specific random.
        if (isProduction)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException(ProductionRequiresStableSecretMessage);
        }

        return jwtSigningKeys.ActiveKey.Material;
    }
}

using System.Security.Cryptography;
using Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Auth;
using Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Autotable;
using Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Changsha.Runtime;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;

namespace Mahjong.Autotable.Api.Tests.Autotable;

/// <summary>
/// Bishop lane, two production seams (report to ripley-3):
/// <list type="bullet">
///   <item><b>B-DEFAULT</b> — Changsha tile-handle privacy is mandatory / default-on with no
///         shippable disable gate (<see cref="ChangshaHandleSecretSource.IsPrivacyOn"/> +
///         <see cref="ChangshaRuntimeOptions.OpaqueHiddenHandles"/> default).</item>
///   <item><b>K-STABLE</b> — the handle secret is a STABLE source: <c>Privacy:HandleSecret</c>
///         preferred, otherwise the stable configured JWT signing key bytes as HKDF IKM; the
///         per-process random fallback is removed; Production fails fast when neither stable source
///         exists, while non-Production follows the existing auth-key convention
///         (<see cref="ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm"/>).</item>
/// </list>
/// RED @200cad4 (default was <c>false</c> + a per-process random fallback); GREEN after.
/// </summary>
public class BishopUatPrivacyDefaultAndKeySourceTests
{
    private const string StableConfiguredKey = "bishop-k-stable-configured-jwt-signing-key-48+bytes!!";

    private static JwtSigningKeyProvider Jwt(params string[] configuredKeys)
        => new(new AuthOptions { JwtSigningKeys = configuredKeys }, NullLogger<JwtSigningKeyProvider>.Instance);

    // ── B-DEFAULT — mandatory / default-on / no shippable disable gate ──

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "B-DEFAULT")]
    public void OpaqueHiddenHandles_DefaultsOn()
        => Assert.True(new ChangshaRuntimeOptions().OpaqueHiddenHandles);

    [Theory, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "B-DEFAULT")]
    // (configuredOn, isProduction) -> effective
    [InlineData(true, false, true)]    // default-on in dev
    [InlineData(false, false, false)]  // dev-only test opt-out is honoured
    [InlineData(false, true, true)]    // Production forces on — NO shippable disable gate
    [InlineData(true, true, true)]
    public void IsPrivacyOn_MandatoryInProduction_DefaultOnElsewhere(bool configuredOn, bool isProd, bool expected)
        => Assert.Equal(expected, ChangshaHandleSecretSource.IsPrivacyOn(configuredOn, isProd));

    // ── K-STABLE — stable secret source, no per-process random ──

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "K-STABLE")]
    public void HandleSecret_IsPreferred_WhenConfigured()
    {
        var secret = RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32);
        var ikm = ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(
            Convert.ToBase64String(secret), Jwt(StableConfiguredKey), isProduction: true);
        Assert.Equal(secret, ikm);
    }

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "K-STABLE")]
    public void StableConfiguredJwtKey_IsUsedAsIkm_WhenNoHandleSecret()
    {
        var jwt = Jwt(StableConfiguredKey);
        Assert.False(jwt.UsingEphemeralFallbackKey);
        var ikm = ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(handleSecretBase64: null, jwt, isProduction: true);
        Assert.Equal(jwt.ActiveKey.Material, ikm);
    }

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "K-STABLE")]
    public void Production_FailsFast_WhenNeitherStableSourceExists()
    {
        var jwt = Jwt(); // empty config ⇒ per-process ephemeral fallback
        Assert.True(jwt.UsingEphemeralFallbackKey);

        var ex = Assert.Throws<InvalidOperationException>(
            () => ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(handleSecretBase64: null, jwt, isProduction: true));
        Assert.Equal(ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ProductionRequiresStableSecretMessage, ex.Message);

        // Empty/whitespace HandleSecret is treated as absent (still throws in Production).
        Assert.Throws<InvalidOperationException>(
            () => ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm("   ", jwt, isProduction: true));
    }

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "K-STABLE")]
    public void NonProduction_FollowsAuthKeyConvention_NoPrivacyRandom_WhenNeitherStableSource()
    {
        var jwt = Jwt(); // dev auth convention: ephemeral per-process key
        var ikm = ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(handleSecretBase64: null, jwt, isProduction: false);

        // It IS the process auth key (NOT a privacy-specific random), and it is stable within the
        // process (deterministic across calls) — proving the per-process privacy random was removed.
        Assert.Equal(jwt.ActiveKey.Material, ikm);
        Assert.Equal(ikm, ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(null, jwt, isProduction: false));
    }

    [Fact, Trait("Category", "UatBackend"), Trait("Contract", "K-STABLE")]
    public void UnusableHandleSecret_DegradesToStableJwtKey()
    {
        var jwt = Jwt(StableConfiguredKey);
        var tooShort = Convert.ToBase64String(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16)); // < 32 bytes
        Assert.Equal(jwt.ActiveKey.Material,
            ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm(tooShort, jwt, isProduction: true));
        Assert.Equal(jwt.ActiveKey.Material,
            ChangshaHandleSecretSource.ResolveIkm("!!not-valid-base64!!", jwt, isProduction: true));
    }
}

### Bishop — F1 dice-anchor oracle: 44 rows, VERIFIED 0-mismatch (for Vasquez sign-off)

**By:** Bishop (bishop-1) · 2026-08-07T15:48:05-07:00 · canonical worktree @200cad4 (integrated).
**Re:** Vasquez F2-primitive ✅ received; this unblocks her F1 (seat,col) dice-anchor oracle.

#### 1. CANONICAL WALL-SIZE FRAME (F1) — DECLARED (single source of truth)
**SEAT-ABSOLUTE `StacksPerSeat = [14, 14, 13, 13]`** (indexed by ABSOLUTE seat, does NOT rotate with dealer):
- Seat 0 → 14 stacks (28 tiles) · Seat 1 → 14 stacks (28 tiles)
- Seat 2 → 13 stacks (26 tiles) · Seat 3 → 13 stacks (26 tiles) · Σ = 108 ✓ (§2.3 "two of 14, two of 13").
This is the ONE frame shared by `BreakPointService.StacksPerSeat` (rules) AND
`AutotableSlotMap.WallStackCount` (render). The former dealer-relative [14,13,14,13] engine frame is COLLAPSED.
(If you named the two candidates P-A/P-B: **P-A = seat-absolute [14,14,13,13] is CHOSEN**; P-B dealer-relative is rejected — it resizes walls as the banker rotates, the F1 drift root cause.)

#### 2. ANCHOR DERIVATION (rules ⇒ render composition)
Given (dealer, diceSum), your rules-owned `BreakPointService.ComputeBreakPoint(diceSum, dealer)` yields
`BreakPointResult(WallIndex, StackIndex, TileIndex)`:
- `wallIndex   = (dealer + (diceSum-1)%4) % 4`            (CCW: 1=dealer,2=right,3=opposite,4=left)
- `stackIndex  = StacksPerSeat[wallIndex] - diceSum`       (count from RIGHT end)

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T15-56] bishop-P0-botdealer-hand1-autoroll-FIXED

#### 2026-08-07T14:20 — Bishop: P0 bot-dealer hand-1 auto-roll stall FIXED (RED→GREEN, full-suite green)

Hudson/Vasquez empirical P0 on exact image `200cad4` (Manual game, human seat 1 + bot dealer seat 0 stalls in RollingDice; human hand stays 0, no pickup). Root-caused + fixed in my lane (`/tmp/mahjong-autotable-uat-backend`, uncommitted). Focused patch: `.squad/decisions/inbox/bishop-backend-P0-botdealer-autoroll.patch` (also folded into the COMPLETE lane patch).

##### Root cause (confirmed by the code's own stale comment)
`ChangshaGameRuntime.StartGameAsync`'s manual branch persisted the fresh `RollingDice` snapshot and `return`ed **without** calling `ScheduleBotIfNeededAsync`. A human dealer rolls via the WS client, but a configured **bot** dealer has no human to press "roll". Only the per-hand re-entry path (`StartNextHandOrEndAsync`, hands 2..N) scheduled the bot-dealer roll — so **hand 1 with a bot dealer never rolled**, and the wall-break + batch-pickup ceremony never began. The old comment in `ScheduleBotIfNeededAsync` even documented the gap: *"StartGameAsync's manual branch never calls ScheduleBotIfNeededAsync, so hand 1 stays client/test-driven."*

##### Fix (minimal, idempotent, no new machinery)
`StartGameAsync` manual branch now calls the EXISTING `ScheduleBotIfNeededAsync(instance, ct)` after releasing the instance lock (same pattern as `RollDiceAsync`/`TakeTilesFromWallAsync`). That method already contains the complete bot-dealer-roll logic:
- fires `RunBotDealerRollAsync` **only** when `Seats[DealerSeatIndex].IsBot` → a **human dealer no-ops**, unchanged client/test-driven roll;
- idempotent via `TryBeginBotSchedule(DealerRoll, dealerSeat)` + `RunBotDealerRollAsync` re-validates `Phase==RollingDice` under the lock → **no duplicate roll** (two-layer guard);
- restructured the manual/auto branch from early-`return` to if/else so the post-lock dispatch runs for Manual too. Updated the now-stale `ScheduleBotIfNeededAsync` comment.

Result: bot dealer auto-rolls hand 1 → drives the pickup chain; a human **non-dealer** receives 13 tiles and gets **interactive pickups** when the cursor reaches their seat (chain halts on the human until their `take`).

##### RED→GREEN proof
New test class `BishopUatBotDealerAutoRollTests` (8 cases):
- `..._HumanNonDealer_ReceivesThirteen_AndInteractivePickups` (human seat 1/2/3, bot dealer 0): asserts phase leaves RollingDice on its own, human hand starts 0 (not auto-dealt), human is the interactive picker for exactly 4 designations → 13 tiles, dealer 14, wall 55, tile-conservation = 108.
- `..._ForEveryDealerPlacement` (dealer 0/1/2/3, all-bot): auto-roll + full self-drive to AwaitingDiscard for every placement.
- `..._IsSingleAndIdempotent_NoDuplicateRoll`: exactly one RollingDice→BreakPointMarked transition for hand 1 (StateChanged counter); a second `RollDiceAsync` post-deal is refused (`InvalidOperationException`) and leaves state untouched.
**Disabling the one-line schedule call → all 8 FAIL by stalling in RollingDice (2m of timeouts).** Restored → all 8 pass.

##### Existing tests updated (the P0 workaround is now redundant)
3 all-bot Manual tests explicitly rolled hand 1's bot dealer to work around this bug; with the fix the runtime auto-rolls, so that explicit `RollDiceAsync(0)` is redundant AND races the scheduled roll (`BotPickupDelayMs=5`/`20`). Removed it from `ResultTombstoneLifecycleTests`, `GameCompleteEmissionTests`, `ManualDealPerHandCeremonyTests` (they now prove auto-roll). The 4 `BotPickupSchedulerAcceptanceTests` keep their explicit rolls — safe (delay ≥50ms head-start; one needs the synchronous roll for a teardown assert).

##### Validation
Targeted (new + affected + adjacent manual-deal): **42/42**. FULL suite (excl. environmental Phase_K_W16/17/18): **Passed 5010, Failed 0, Skipped 2** (was 5002 → +8). Build 0 errors.

##### Ownership / integration note
Backend production + tests, my lane. This stacks cleanly on my F1/F2/targetSlots/SC-2 patch (only `ChangshaGameRuntime.cs` overlaps and is additive). Frost/ripley-3: apply the COMPLETE lane patch (contains this P0) for the canonical build.

## [Archived from inbox 2026-08-07T15-56] ripley-sc2-wire-key-contract-verified

### Ripley — SC-2 `things` wire-key contract VERIFIED (number=real | string=opaque)

**When:** 2026-08-07T13:22-07:00
**By:** Ripley (Lead/integration coordinator)
**Re:** Pinning the exact SC-2/G19 `things` key wire types after Hicks flagged a discriminator ambiguity. Verified read-only in `/tmp/mahjong-autotable-uat-backend`. Supersedes the imprecise "numeric-string 0..107" phrasing in my 10:44 wire note.

#### The verified contract (authoritative)
Each `things` entry is `["things", <key>, <ThingInfo>]`. The key is:
- **VISIBLE (entitled) tile** ⇒ JSON **NUMBER** `0..107` (the real Changsha tileId). Client resolves face via `floor(realId/4)`.
- **HIDDEN tile** (foreign concealed hand, all wall, foreign concealed kong) ⇒ JSON **STRING** `h_<base64url>` (opaque per-viewer HKDF handle). No rank/suit derivable.

#### Evidence (`AutotableProtocol.cs` CollectionEntryJsonConverter)
- **Write** (~:731+): `switch(value.Key){ case string s: WriteStringValue(s); case int i: WriteNumberValue(i); case long l: WriteNumberValue(l); }` ⇒ opaque handle serializes as a JSON string, real tileId as a JSON number. (`BuildThingEntry:705` sets `key = privacy.Key(tileId, hidden)` = `hidden ? Handle(tileId) : tileId` = string | int.)
- **Read** (~:698-709): a JSON number boxes as `long`; comment explicitly warns the backend's own `TryHandleDiscardActionAsync`/`TryHandleClaimActionAsync` do `entry.Key is long` — a stringified visible key would fall through and be rejected as a bad seat.

#### Consequence — a HARD invariant
Visible keys MUST be JSON numbers on BOTH ends: the backend's action matching depends on `is long`, and the client's face resolution depends on int-parsing. There is NO legitimate numeric-STRING visible key on the wire. The contract is strictly **`number(real 0..107)` | `string(h_ opaque)`**.

#### Hicks client — CONFIRMED CORRECT against this
Hicks replaced a fragile `typeof key === 'string'` discriminator (which would have mis-flagged a numeric-string "0" as opaque) with value-based `parseRealTileId`: REAL ⟺ int-parses to 0..107 (number or numeric-string, normalized to number); OPAQUE ⟺ else (`h_…`/non-numeric/out-of-range). Applied to isOpaqueHandle, resolveTileFace (face from entitled realId, never the key), partitionThingEntries (real keys normalized to number ⇒ world numeric path byte-identical), move-log/replay onThings. tsc --strict clean; 132 browser-free contract tests + 3 new numeric-string cases; ESLint clean; no dist rebuild/commit. The tolerated numeric-string case is defensive headroom, not the literal format — kept as robustness.

#### Gates must assert these exact types
- **Hudson live P1 (raw-WS):** visible entries carry a JSON NUMBER 0..107; hidden entries carry a JSON STRING `h_…`. (Plus the emission-ORDER assertion already routed: hidden partition slot-canonical, never tileId-sorted.)
- **Frost whitelist:** BuildThingEntry key type = number|string per above (already reviewed correct); no `face` field.
- **SC-4 pickup unaffected/orthogonal:** `targetSlots` len-1 public slot names; opaque handles are ONLY the hidden `things` render key, never the pickup match.

#### (b) THREE-WAY — reachability vs emission-presence at the single-pickups (49/51 load-bearing)
**Correction (Frost RV2 emission-behavior verify, Vasquez code-confirmed 2026-08-07):** the
prior header conflated OCCLUSION (present-but-not-reachable) with CONSUMPTION (drawn → absent
from `things`). They are distinct axes and must not share an "ABSENT/tombstoned" label.

Code fact (`ChangshaToAutotableTranslator.cs` wall loop ~L669-676): the translator emits **one
`thing` per `state.Wall[i]`** — i.e. for **every UNDRAWN tile** — with `hidden:true`. Privacy
opacifies the tile VALUE (face-down opaque handle); the SLOT is **never dropped**. Only a **DRAWN**
tile (removed from `state.Wall`) leaves `things`. So an undrawn-but-occluded bottom is
PRESENT-in-things, merely **not reachable** (≠ `targetSlots[0]`). `ComputeWallFrontSlots` (~L516-539)
co-derives the same `wallFrontSlots` list for both `things` and `pickup.targetSlots`
(`frontDrawn = 108 − Wall.Count − WallBackDrawn`), so the two cannot diverge.

The SC-3 (b) test must therefore assert THREE things, not a two-column present/absent:

| frontDrawn | REACHABLE (== targetSlots[0], the (a) literal) | ABSENT-from-`things` (DRAWN/consumed) | PRESENT-in-`things` but NOT reachable (occluded) |
|-----------:|:-----------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| 48         | wall.5.1@2 (top)                                | —                                     | wall.5.0@2 (bottom, undrawn, occluded by its top) |
| **49**     | wall.5.0@2 (bottom)                             | **wall.5.1@2** (top drawn 48→49)      | —                                                |
| 50         | wall.6.1@2 (top)                                | —                                     | wall.6.0@2 (bottom, undrawn, occluded by its top) |
| **51**     | wall.6.0@2 (bottom)                             | **wall.6.1@2** (top drawn 50→51)      | —                                                |

- **Assertion 1 (all 17 states):** emitted `targetSlots[0]` == the (a) literal — top-first reachability.
- **Assertion 2 (ABSENT/up-link-empty, load-bearing):** ONLY the drawn tops are absent from `things` —
  fd49→`wall.5.1@2`, fd51→`wall.6.1@2`. This is the genuine tombstone/consumption catcher (≡ BishopUat #2).
- **Assertion 3 (occlusion, do NOT mislabel absent):** the even bottoms fd48→`wall.5.0@2`,
  fd50→`wall.6.0@2` are PRESENT in `things` (opaque) and NOT reachable (≠ `targetSlots[0]`).
  Asserting them "absent from `things`" would **false-RED the correct top-first emission** — the trap.

A `layer==1` assertion would falsely RED 49/51 (reachable layer-0 bottoms); the up-link-empty form
(reachable ⇔ front of the remaining arc, its sibling either drawn-and-absent or undrawn-and-occluded)
GREENs them. Rules content (which layer is reachable) is unchanged from the original memo — only the
emission-presence LABEL is corrected.

#### FRAMING SUPERSESSION (important)
My earlier single literal `Slot(49)=(1,10,0)` was an **absolute-ordinal** demonstration
(`WallOrdinalToSlot(49)` directly), used only to illustrate the top-first mapping primitive.
It is **NOT** a deal-bound frontier: no legal deal breaks at flat index 0
(`col = 14 − sum = 0 ⇒ sum = 14`, impossible), so `frontDrawn=49` never resolves to
`wall.10.0@1` in a real ceremony. For the SC-3 real-emission test, the **deal-bound**
table above (break-indexed from `TileIndex=18`) is authoritative; the absolute-ordinal form
is retired for this purpose.

#### Provenance (non-circular)
These 17 literals were derived TWO independent ways that agree byte-for-byte:
1. **Rules** (§2.4 physical perimeter): from the break stack, draw increasing-col,
   top-before-bottom, CCW-wrap at each seat's col-max into the next seat's col0.

#### 1. Frame (locked, seat-absolute, NON-rotating)

- `StacksPerSeat = [14,14,13,13]` by ABSOLUTE seat (seats 0,1 = 14 stacks; seats 2,3 = 13).
- Broken seat: `B = (dealer + (sum−1) mod 4) mod 4`  (1=dealer, 2=right, 3=opposite, 4=left, wrapping).
- Break column (impl / R1): `col = N − sum`, where `N = StacksPerSeat[B]`.
- Layer: `1` (TOP) — break ordinal is always even ⇒ Wall[0] is the reachable exposed top (F2).

#### 2. Egocentric physical convention (code-verified — Frost Part-A `makeSlots` ≡ this)

Sit at seat B, facing the table centre:

- **`col N−1` (col-max) = your RIGHT end** (corner abutting the NEXT player CCW, seat B+1).
- The renderer places seat B's col-max corner adjacent to seat B+1's wall (verified: seat0
  col+x→bottom-right→seat1; seat1 col-max→top→seat2). Handedness is INDEX-based (B+1),
  independent of the E/S/W/N wind label (winds rotate with the dealer; geometry does not).

**Break location:** count `sum` stacks from your RIGHT end (col-max) leftward; the `sum`-th
stack is the break stack (col `N−sum`). Its TOP tile is drawn first.

**Depletion DIRECTION (code-verified, numeric):** from the break, the wall depletes
**increasing-col** (top-then-bottom within each stack), i.e. moving BACK toward your RIGHT
end (col-max), then wraps **counter-clockwise** into seat B+1's wall at its `col 0` (LEFT)
end, and continues around the perimeter as one contiguous arc. Verified draw runs:
- dealer0/sum5 → `(0,9,1)→(0,9,0)→(0,10,1)→(0,10,0)→…`
- dealer0/sum2 → `(1,12,1)→(1,12,0)→(1,13,1)→(1,13,0)→(2,0,1)…`  (wraps seat1 col-max → seat2 col0)

This is the "single sequential remaining run from the break" the user demanded — NOT the
four-half-walls scatter. Gate must assert a CONTIGUOUS depleted arc, not per-seat no-gap.

#### 6. §2.4 PROSE DRAFT (worked example + diagram, egocentric right/left) — DRAFT, hold final until (a) picked

> Placeholder `⟨col⟩` below = `N − sum` if the user confirms impl (R1), or `N − sum − 1` if

##### 2.4.2 Worked example + egocentric break diagram (draft)

Rolling determines the broken wall and stack by counting from the roller's seat:

1. **Broken seat.** `B = (dealer + (sum−1) mod 4) mod 4`. Counting CCW from the dealer:
   sum≡1→dealer's own wall, 2→right-hand seat, 3→opposite, 0(≡4)→left-hand seat.
2. **Break stack.** Facing the table from seat B, your wall runs `col 0` (LEFT corner, toward
   seat B−1) to `col N−1` (RIGHT corner, toward seat B+1). Count `sum` stacks from your RIGHT
   corner leftward; the `sum`-th stack — column **⟨col⟩** — is the break. Its TOP tile is
   drawn first.
3. **Depletion.** Draw proceeds from the break toward your RIGHT corner (increasing column,
   top-of-stack before bottom), then wraps counter-clockwise into seat B+1's wall at that
   seat's LEFT corner (`col 0`), continuing as one contiguous arc around the perimeter.

**Worked example — dealer 0, dice sum 5.** `B = (0 + 4 mod 4) mod 4 = 0` (dealer breaks his
OWN wall). `N = 14`. Count 5 stacks from seat 0's RIGHT corner: the break is column
**⟨9⟩** (impl) [or **⟨8⟩** strict]. First-removed = `(seat 0, col 9, top)`; the wall then
empties col 9→10→11→12→13 (top then bottom each), wrapping CCW to seat 1's col 0.

```
              seat 2  (top, 13 stacks, col0=its LEFT)
      col-max ┌───────────────┐ col0
   (→seat3)   │   . . . . . . │   (→seat1)
   seat 3 ┌───┤               ├───┐ seat 1
  (13 st) │   │    TABLE      │   │ (14 st)
   col0   │   │    CENTRE     │   │  col-max
 (→seat2) └───┤               ├───┘ (→seat2)
   col0       │ . . B* . . . .│ col-max
   (→seat3)   └───────────────┘ (→seat1)
      seat 0 (bottom, dealer, 14 stacks)
      LEFT=col0 ........ RIGHT=col13
      B* = break col 9 (dealer0/sum5); depletes → toward RIGHT (col13), wraps CCW to seat1 col0
```
Egocentric: "count `sum` from YOUR RIGHT; the run opens there and empties toward your right
corner, then to the player on your right."
